# VAML ROADMAP — S000..S999 (authoritative tokenized step list)

> This is THE step enumeration for VAML. It was originally framed as a "POC," but it stopped being one
> before S001 — per the standing decision (ADR-017), this is **v1 built at v2 quality** ("version 2 as our
> first version"): a real production first version, not a throwaway to be ported. `progress.md` (repo root)
> is the continuation file that tracks completion. This file is the source of WHAT to do; each step has a token
> `S###`, a dependency (`dep:`), and a one-line description. The "no-stub" rule applies: a step
> is only ✅ when its behavior is real and verified by build + tests.
>
> Sprint headers list the sprint's goal. Token ranges reserve room; gaps mean reserved headroom
> for steps discovered mid-execution (append new steps into the nearest open token, then renumber
> the tail in one pass — do NOT edit the checkpoint by hand

the roadmap MUST ALWAYS be updated before informing user the status is DONE.

## GUARD RAILS (operative project contracts — codified from S003 forward)
### MINIMAL REAL (official term)
- A small, **permanent**, linkable public symbol that seeds a component's true interface (e.g. a
  version marker). Distinct from a **STUB**: a STUB is throwaway scaffold deleted later; MINIMAL
  REAL is **kept and extended** into the real implementation. It is NOT lazy — it is a deliberate,
  declared, forward-resolvable seed.
- Every MINIMAL REAL symbol carries a **searchable sentinel comment**:
  `// [MINIMAL REAL] <component> — RESOLVED BY <sprint-token>. Do NOT extend silently; do NOT backfill.`
- A MINIMAL REAL symbol may ONLY be removed or replaced by the step that **explicitly declares**
  its resolution.
- Active MINIMAL REAL marks (searchable): ~~`vaml-vulkan` version marker → **RESOLVED BY S161**~~ —
  **RESOLVED at S161** (the marker was replaced by the real Vulkan/GLFW surface: PlatformWindow at
  S160 + the Vulkan/VMA linkage at S161; the real `version()` symbol is kept and extended, sentinel
  tag removed there).
  `vaml-tools` version marker → ~~**RESOLVED BY S287**~~ — **RESOLVED at S287** (the S287 embed/compiler
  work replaced the marker with the real tooling surface: version.h sentinel tag removed, the real
  `vaml::tools::version()/Version/tools_name()` symbol KEPT + EXTENDED as the version of the now-real
  vamlcc/embed/VBamlReader lib); built-in element seeds (S087, in `vaml/core/Element.h`)
  → each resolved by its OWN control/layout sprint: `StackPanel` → **S129 (RESOLVED — re-based onto
  UIElement as a real panel)**, `Grid` → **S131 (RESOLVED — re-based onto UIElement as a real
  panel: row/col definitions + Absolute/Auto/Star resolution + attached Grid.Row/Grid.Column)**,
  `WrapPanel` → **S134 (RESOLVED — REAL panel authored at S134; a NEW element, not a seed)**,
  `Canvas` → **S136 (RESOLVED — REAL panel authored at S136; a NEW element, not a seed; explicit
  Left/Top attached DPs, NaN default)**,
  `Button` → **S401**, `Text` → **S400**,
  `TextBox` → **S402**, `CheckBox` → **S404**, `Slider` → **S403**, `ScrollViewer` → **S405**,
  `Window` → **S440**;
  VamlReader event hooks (S092, in `vaml/core/VamlReader.h`) → **RESOLVED at S322** (the S322 markup
  event wiring replaced the seed with the real surface: `register_event`, `deferred_event_handlers`,
  `bind_class_handler` + `BindEvents`; the sentinel tag was removed at that step — kept + extended,
  never backfilled).
  `DependencyProperty::TryGetByName`/`GetByName` (S801, the guarded unique-name read bridge over the
  composite store) → **RESOLVED BY S803** (the reader dotted-key → first-class composite; S803 retires
  the bridge when no call site can lack an owner).
  (The `Color` + `Thickness` marks, both previously **RESOLVED BY S089**, are RESOLVED as of S089 —
  their real parsing semantics now live on the types via parse_color/parse_thickness, and their
  sentinel tags were removed at that step.)

### NO-GAP GUARANTEE (official term)
- Binding project contract: **no feature or symbol may be left behind for a silent backfill step.**
  Anything introduced as MINIMAL REAL must have an explicit, scheduled resolution point, recorded
  in the roadmap AND progress tracking, authored at the SAME step that delivers the real content.
- Any future step that uses MINIMAL REAL carries an obligation: it must be **searchable and
  resolvable** by its named sprint. Resolution is part of the real feature's own step, never a
  separate cleanup/backfill step.
- Forward-declared resolutions (contracts): ~~**S161 must resolve the vulkan MINIMAL REAL marker**~~
  (**RESOLVED at S161** — Sprint 4 delivered PlatformWindow + CMake Vulkan/VMA linkage + removed the
  vulkan sentinel); **S287 must resolve the tools MINIMAL REAL marker. S089 HAS resolved the Color + Thickness
  MINIMAL REAL markers (introduced by S030) — parse_color + parse_thickness authored at S089,
  sentinel tags removed there; no backfill.**

### NO LAZY LLM SYNDROME (official term)
- The project's default reasoning posture. When in doubt, **reason the opposite of lazy LLM**:
  prefer the explicit, the searchable, the contractually-bound, and the non-silent option.
- **MINIMAL REAL is explicitly NOT lazy-LLM** — it is a strategic choice made to keep resolution
  steps coherent **by design**, justified and recorded in this documentation, never a shortcut
  taken for convenience.

### RENDER SURFACE CONFORMANCE — `docs/RENDER_SURFACE.md` (operative project contract, baked from S11f)
- `docs/RENDER_SURFACE.md` is the **XAML render-model → VAML Vulkan surface** catalog: every XAML/WPF visual
  concept maps to a Vulkan material + primitive with a tri-state (**REAL / VERTICAL-SLICE / PLACEHOLDER / GAP**)
  + its **NO-GAP resolution token**. It is transcribed from the CURRENT `classify_merge_element` reality
  (`src/presentation/src/VamlRenderer.cpp`) — NOT a rewrite plan and NOT a runtime-behavior change.
- The conformance validator `src/presentation/tools/render_surface_check.py` enforces: **every classifier arm
  MUST have a row in the matrix**, and **every non-REAL row MUST name its NO-GAP token**. A new control can no
  longer land a render path that is invisible/un-catalogued (the anti-blank-splash / anti-single-box guard).
- **CONFORMANCE OBLIGATION (baked, not optional):** ANY sprint that introduces or changes a renderable surface
  MUST update the matrix row + re-run the validator **at that same step** (per NO-GAP / NO-LAZY-LLM), never as a
  silent backfill. The catalog is authored **global-impact-first** (S11f = the first render-inert sprint that
  conforms to it): roadmap tokens below reference it from birth.
- This is **not** a type DAG: the type-inheritance catalog stays `docs/DAG_controls.md` (11k-0); RENDER_SURFACE
  is the orthogonal *render-surface* map. Naming is XAML→Vulkan (there is **no DirectX** in the repo — the
  renderer is native Vulkan, per ADR-011/ADR-019).

### LOCK GOVERNANCE — ADR-018 (operative project contract)
- **ONLY the human architect may approve ANY use of a lock/mutex/semaphore/etc.** in this codebase.
- An agent/LLM introducing a lock must (a) surface it as an explicit review item with rationale (why
  it cannot be avoided), (b) obtain the human architect's approval, and (c) mark the lock site with
  a searchable comment naming the approval.
- **Locks are never hidden:** every cross-thread lock is declared in the public/docs surface so
  callers can plan around it.
- **Standing pre-approved lock: NONE in the DP value/notification layer.** [STRIKED + REVISED BY 11t S812 — the S037/S041 per-thread ChangeQueue pending-queue mutex NO LONGER EXISTS and is NO LONGER pre-approved. WPF has no DP value queue, no DP notification queue, and no change coalescer — the only DP notification is the synchronous `PropertyMetadata.PropertyChangedCallback` (DO.cs:2039) — so `SetResult::QUEUED`, the S041 `ChangeQueue` mutex, the S041`ChangeProcessor`, and the S038/S042 `ChangeRecorder` coalescer are all DELETED by 11t S811. There is therefore NO pre-approved DP-value lock and NO "notification ChangeQueue" lock to carry forward. The ONE cross-thread lock + change-log that remains in the pipeline is the **11n-4 `CollectionView` opt-in fill→drain deque + swap mutex** (`_changeLogLock`, `CollectionView.cs:1878–1929`, gated on opt-in `AllowsCrossThreadChanges`) — a DECISION-2 human-approved exception, IN-LIBRARY, never a DP-value channel and never a DP-notification channel. All other locks require the approval gate.]
- **Sprint 3.5 adds ZERO new locks by design** — the intern subsystem (S141/S140_1/S140) is
  thread-local lockless, S145's object block pool is thread-local + lockless (thread-affine per S037,
  so it needs NO lock), and S146's HeapStats is a relaxed atomic (no mutex). The ONLY lock action in
  Sprint 3.5 was S143's relocation of the standing pre-approved S037/S041 ChangeQueue mutex (moved, not
  created). [STRIKED + REVISED BY 11t S812 — that S143-relocated ChangeQueue mutex MOVED WITH the S041 queue that 11t S811 deleted; the S143 relocation note is rewritten to "moved OUT of the DP layer entirely." The S143 content-keyed NameTable re-key half (S140/S141 store) is queue-independent and survives.] Any future lock (e.g. S620 async layout) requires the same approval gate. Recorded in
  `adr/ADR-LOG.md` as ADR-018.

## Conventions
- `dep:S00X` = this step requires S00X complete first. Multiple deps separated by `+`.
- `dep:-` = no dependency (root step of its sprint).
- Gates: each sprint ends with a `REFACTOR GATE` step (force `-G` in the token's line) that removes
  dead code and re-verifies full build (MSVC + Clang) + ctest.
- Layer rule: `src/core` NEVER depends on Vulkan/GLFW; only `src/vulkan` may. Enforced by CMake.
- Distribution: consumer chooses shared/static; default static. [ADR-003]
- **VIEWER GROWTH (official term — the "always updated" contract, enforceable, NOT prose):** the
  vaml_viewer (S220+) is the PERMANENT visual-feedback vehicle — the app's face. Its reload loop
  (S222_1) re-runs the whole S5 path with ZERO imperative tree-building ("render live VAML like an app
  would, without a code-behind"). COMPLETION GATE: a sprint named in the viewer-growth table (below) is
  NOT DONE until its viewer-growth token is demonstrated in the LIVE viewer — no token, no ✅, same as
  no green lane (the anti-grave-whistle clause). MARKER: each affected sprint header + progress.md
  carries a `VIEWER GROWTH:` line — a recorded, carried state, never assumed. The viewer is
  PREVIEW-ONLY (pan/zoom on the rendered view); there is NO embedded source editor (no distraction from
  the core mission; edits happen in any external editor + live reload). The viewer is NOT built for the
  throwaway POCs (S220 deletes both); it is the single surviving vehicle that consumes ONLY the public
  surface.

## Sprint 3.5 — Allocation & ownership discipline (retrofit of S0–S3 hot paths)  [token S140+]
> RATIONALE (reasoning agreement, latest who/what/why): eliminate the two orthogonal sources of heap
> churn in the shipped hot paths before the renderer (S210/S211) and binding engine (S240+) are built on
> them. (1) OBJECT churn: per-object make_unique<Impl>() + per-node unordered_map lifts; (2) STRING churn:
> transient std::string(id.name()) materialized per lookup. Both removed by: a token-keyed (string_view)
> CONTENT-keyed SIMD probe store (THREAD-LOCAL, LOCKLESS — ADR-018) + a thread-local retain-forever
> block pool (the object-side half, S145) + interned/string_view keys. Equality is by CONTENT (SIMD
> full compare), NEVER pointer-identity — a caller's address is never a usable pre-check (their bytes
> are not in the pool), and cross-thread interned views are content-compared. The earlier
> pointer-identity / global-lock framing is REJECTED (ADR-018).
> Retrofit rule agreed: past steps are REWRITTEN in place to the intended end-state (no deadwood, no
> "historical record" preservation); SOLID/release discipline (freeze + annotate) begins only at first release.
> RATIONALE CORRECTION (ADR-003 revised + ADR-019): the pimpl's original "ABI / IP-hiding / closed ABI
> surface" justification is a LEFTOVER from a shared/DLL distribution model — this MIT-public lib is
> statically linked with no runtime ABI boundary to defend (see architecture §7, artifact-model.cmake,
> DependencyObject.h — all revised in place). The pimpl survives only as a speed liability; S142 collapses
> it (pimpl removed, not preserved) for SPEED (trampoline + per-object heap hop on the CPU Get/Set/cascade
> path), which the CPU/GPU line (ADR-019) requires.
>
> Store contract (agreed spec): non-owning `string_view` key, UTF-8 canonical, pure C++. Insertion-ordered
> append-only array; SIMD-probe on 32-byte groups (AVX2, no AVX-512) of 8-bit search bytes; empty marker 0xFF;
> probe byte = fold_bytes(sv) (rotating-XOR over bytes) % 255; growth = memmove+append rounded up to a
> 32-entry group, never re-probe / reorder / shrink; erase/tombstone never applies (append-only); full
> string_view compare disambiguates collisions; index<n bounds the scan to the used prefix. One PD type
> (no common/root), no unordered_map/flat_hash_map, no pimpl heap node (store is block-resident), retain-
> forever free-list, thread-local pool (ADR-018: LOCKLESS — each thread owns its store; zero locks, zero
> deadlock surface), opt-in master destroy_all(). The intern pool is PUBLIC — it is the
> `vaml::intern(string_view) -> string_view` retained-string primitive (S140_1), usable by internal hot paths
> AND external programmers alike: probe the CALLING THREAD's SIMD store BY VALUE; on HIT return the existing
> view (content-dedup); on MISS retain the bytes into the thread-local pool, insert into the store, return the
> new view. SINGLE by-value call (`intern`); NO by-reference/pointer variant, NO reverse-index auto-conversion
> — reserved only for a future consumer that authors its own address shortcut AT ITS OWN STEP (S620,
> measure-first). Equality is by CONTENT (SIMD), NEVER pointer-identity — the caller's address is not a
> usable pre-check, and cross-thread interned views are compared by content only. LIFETIME CONTRACT
> (rewritten): the caller is NOT required to outlive us — anything that flows through intern() is retained for
> the LIFE OF THE INTERNING THREAD (once in, always there, never removed, never relocated); do NOT pass an
> interned view ACROSS threads — carry literals/owned strings across threads instead. WARNING (stated, not
> hidden): persistent retention is unbounded and reclaimed-never per thread — do NOT call intern() on
> unbounded or unpredictable-valued data (only bounded vocabulary + parsed document text). We consume intern()
> ourselves for BOTH identity keys AND parser/reader-produced tree text. Symbolic/team-fidelity: names stay as
> programmers know them; token derived 1:1 at intern time, never redefined.

  (B) THE TOOLKIT-ANALOG FREE TEMPLATE `template <typename T> bool set_property(ObservableObject&, PropertyId, T& field, const T& new_value)` — REAL-CHANGE-ONLY: returns false when `field == new_value` (no store write, no signal); on a real change it assigns `field` AND calls `obj.Set(id, to_value(new_value))` — firing the GENUINE S241 typed PropertyChanged (id, old, new) from the ObservableObject store. The bounded payload types all carry value `==`; a T without it fails to compile together with the to_value guard (never a silent no-change).
  (C) `PROPERTY_BINDABLE(TYPE, NAME)` — expands inside a class deriving vaml::ObservableObject to `private TYPE NAME_field_ = TYPE{};` + `const TYPE& NAME() const noexcept` getter + `bool set_NAME(const TYPE&)` (wiring set_property). Accessor naming matches the repo convention (orientation()/set_orientation()). Property NAME bound via `PropertyId::of(#Name)` — a string literal (compile-time, no registry, no collision class).
  FIELD ↔ STORE SYNC CONTRACT (documented in the header): the typed backing field is the C++ source of truth; `set_property` keeps the ObservableObject Value store in lock-step so `observable_object_reader()->Get(name)` (S240/S241) and the S242 binding engine read the live value. A bindable property is written ONLY through its generated `set_<Name>` setter (the base ObservableObject::Set remains for manual/non-bindable props; writing base Set directly for a bindable name would desync the field mirror — the documented footgun, the setter is the canonical path).
  NO change to ObservableObject (the S241 shipped surface stays fixed). NO new library target (header-only, compiled into vaml-core), NO new lock (ADR-018: a bindable property is written on the VM's owner thread, mirrors ObservableObject). NO MINIMAL REAL introduced/resolved. NO-GAP: S256 (viewer growth) consumes this convenience layer when the viewer populates a VM. [VIEWER GROWTH: S256]

## VIEWER-GROWTH CONVENTION (baked from S5a/S6 forward — the binding rule, now enforceable)
The vaml_viewer's reload loop (S222_1) is the PERMANENT visual-feedback vehicle. Every sprint that introduces
a renderable feature MUST either flow through the generic renderer automatically (it does — the viewer is a
GENERIC renderer over the public surface) or carry a NAMED viewer-growth token in that sprint. COMPLETION GATE
(the anti-grave-whistle clause): a sprint named in the viewer-growth table is NOT DONE until its viewer-growth
token is demonstrated in the LIVE viewer — no token, no ✅, same as no green lane. MARKER: each affected sprint
header + progress.md carries a `VIEWER GROWTH:` line so the update is a recorded, carried state, never assumed.
The viewer is PREVIEW-ONLY (pan/zoom), NO embedded source editor (no distraction from the core mission).

**OPEN-ENDED (no "past the list" hole — the gate does NOT end at S10):** the completion gate applies to EVERY
sprint that introduces a renderable feature, for the WHOLE road (S11 through S18 and beyond, to S989), not just
the enumerated tokens up to S10. The table below is a NON-EXHAUSTIVE exemplar, not a closed list. This closes
the lazy-LLM escape route of "the list stops at S10, so no growth is owed after it": (a) EVERY Sprint-11+
SURVIVOR + checkpoint MUST carry a `VIEWER GROWTH:` line (present even when it says "no new renderable feature
this sprint — viewer unchanged; RELOAD still demonstrated"); and (b) any sprint that DOES add a renderable
feature MUST add a named viewer-growth token in that same sprint, on penalty of not being DONE (same as no
green lane).

### Notes on edge cases (so you don't get surprises)
- RichTextBox — has a real closure, but it's 11k_12, which sits outside the 11aa–bz range. If you count any correction (not just 11aa–bz), it's already closed and can be dropped; under the strict "11aa-bz" test it stays.
- TextBlock — only partially touched (11k-1 re-base, 11ap FontSize default). No full per-control corrective like TextBox/Button got. Needs a dedicated audit.
- Window — only partially closed (11bd: non-routed Closing; Sprint 11o: transparency; 11k-9: DP set). No single consolidated Window corrective. Needs one.
- UserControl — resolved as an element at 11j-1 + re-bound at 11k-11, but no 11a–bz per-control corrective. Keep if auditing to the corrective baseline.
- ListBox / ListView — 11bj re-homed the shared Selector items model, but S473 itself has no corrective sprint ("forward hand-off recorded, not re-litigated"). Keep for a dedicated audit.
- Canvas / Grid / StackPanel / WrapPanel — these are already-REAL panels (S129–S136), so the "audit" here is a WPF-drift re-audit, not a missing implementation. They're still not covered by any 11aa–bz sprint, so they remain on the list.

> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (recorded frankly, NOT a defensible dodge):** a fidelity error was made in the
> initial control list — `Text` is NOT a WPF control (WPF has `TextBlock` and `TextBox`; no
> `System.Windows.Controls.Text` exists). It was authored as a seed at S087 and "resolved" as a real control
> at S400 under an INVENTED name, contrary to the standing directive of fidelity to XAML. The WPF-corpus
> load dump exposed the consequence directly: `vaml_viewer: unknown element type '<TextBlock>'` across
> ~10 corpus files (AddPhysicianWindow/MainWindow/InitialViewUserControl/StatusBoard/SplashUserControl/
> MagneticSystemStatusControl/PreferLocationIndicator/ShadowLocationIndicator/etc.) — i.e. the most common
> WPF text control does not even load in vaml_viewer. Sprint 11j closed the *load-surface* gaps
> (elements/DPs/values/doc-level) but never audited the **control-NAME set** against WPF, which is the root
> cause. This sprint is the correction + the disclosure of what was omitted. It follows the **S167_1
> corrective-token convention** (supersede in place, history stays intact, no renumber) — NOT a rewrite of
> history and NOT a silent backfill.
>
> **THE FIDELITY CONTRACT (sealed by the closing gate, 11k-7):** from this sprint onward, every authored
> element/control name MUST exist in real WPF (the registered built-in + classified control names are
> checked against the WPF type namespace — a name with no WPF type is a defect, not a new element). NO
> invented control names, ever. A corpus doc that loads a control NOT in WPF is a bug in VAML, not a new
> element.

> **DECISION (11n-2 / DAG — recorded at plan review, accepted by the driver):** the command object is the
> EXISTING single `vaml::ICommand` (S246) family — there is NO second/parallel ICommand and NO bridge.
> WPF has exactly one `ICommand`; `RoutedCommand : ICommand`, `RelayCommand : ICommand`, and every button
> holds that one interface. 11n-2 therefore EXTENDS the S246 family:
> - `RoutedCommand : vaml::ICommand` (implements Execute/CanExecute/CanExecuteChanged by raising a routed
>   command event — WPF-true behavior, no delegate),
> - `CommandManager` = the routed-command registry/hook (the object-level analogue of the S253 name
>   registry),
> - `ICommandSource` formalizes the `Command`/`CommandParameter`/`CommandTarget` DP trait ButtonBase already
>   half-has,
> - `ButtonBase.Command` DP UPGRADED from string to `vaml::ICommand*` — the string `Command="Save"` remains
>   SUGAR resolving through the S253/S464 registry; `Command="{Binding SaveCommand}"` binds the real object
>   directly,
> - `InputBinding : Freezable, ICommandSource -> KeyBinding/MouseBinding` + `InputGesture -> KeyGesture/MouseGesture`.
> Rationale (the driver's "for dummies" review): the S246 header already claims to BE the WPF
> `System.Windows.Input.ICommand`-analogue, so a second parallel family would collide at the type level and
> force a bridge WPF does not have; unifying keeps existing `vaml::RelayCommand` ViewModels binding to buttons
> unchanged (no usability regression), matches WPF's single-interface design, and satisfies the roadmap's
> stated "real command object" goal with ZERO name collision. Recorded NO-GAP: the S246 `ICommand` +
> `RelayCommand` and the S253/S464 string-registry surface are REUSED, never re-pointed or duplicated.

## 11n-4 — BINDINGBASE + IMultiValueConverter + CollectionView + OBSERVABLE COLLECTIONS — **OPTION A (WPF-fidelity event subscription)**
The reactive spine (the substantial observable-collection infrastructure VAML lacks -> landed HERE):
- `INotifyPropertyChanged` / `INotifyCollectionChanged` / `NotifyCollectionChangedEventArgs` (+
  `CollectionChangedAction` enum) — the notification interfaces.
- `ObservableCollection<T>` (VAML-native, over a heterogeneous `Value::Collection`) raising
  `PropertyChanged("Count"/"Item[]")` + `CollectionChanged` on every mutation.
- `BindingBase` (a MarkupExtension) -> `Binding` / `MultiBinding` / `PriorityBinding`; `BindingExpression`
  subscribes via `IWeakEventListener` (the weak-handler subscription-lifetime contract) and RE-RUNS on
  `PropertyChanged` / `CollectionChanged` (true event-subscription, WPF-faithful — NOT polled).
- `CollectionView : DispatcherObject, ICollectionView, INotifyPropertyChanged` — the live collection read
  model under `ItemsControl`.
- `ItemsControl` incrementally adds/removes containers on `CollectionChanged`.
- **ROADMAP NOTE (per directive, recorded verbatim in the roadmap 11n-4):** this step works CLOSELY WITH A
  HUMAN for the locking/threading reasoning. **Locks can be engineered out, but not always.** Single-threaded
  UI paths avoid locks; the subscription-lifetime weak-handler re-entrancy (a collection mutated mid-
  enumeration inside a callback) is where a lock may be unavoidable — that decision is made WITH A HUMAN,
  never silently. ADR-018 is deliberately renegotiated here with human sign-off.

> **DECISION-2 (11n-4 — the human-gated ADR-018 renegotiation, RESOLVED with the driver at plan review):**
> the reactive spine is **lock-free by default**; locks are allowed **ONLY behind an explicit opt-in** —
> mirroring WPF's `AllowsCrossThreadChanges`, verified against the WPF source.
> - **THE CHANGE LOG (codified):** the framework owns the collection-view change log as **two deques:
>   `filling` and `draining`** (WPF `_changeLog`/`_tempChangeLog`, `CollectionView.cs:1900-1941`). Filling
>   collects pending changes; draining processes them. On opt-in, the fill→drain **swap** happens under the
>   one permitted mutex (WPF `_changeLogLock`, `CollectionView.cs:2125`); draining itself runs outside the
>   lock.
> - **`AllowsCrossThreadChanges` (codified):** a per-view OPT-IN, defaulting to **false**. Default `false`
>   (WPF `CollectionView.cs:81/1162`): cross-thread producers are REJECTED at the collection boundary — a
>   WPF-style `NotSupportedException` throw-guard, NOT a queue and NOT a lock. Opt-in `true`: cross-thread
>   producers are allowed to FILL the filling deque; the APP owns its own thread-pool / async (injected via
>   the S540 `IUiExecutor` / 11z pump seam — the framework does NOT own or impose a dispatcher/InvokeAsync)
>   and is responsible for all OTHER race conditions beyond the framework's own change log.
> - **DRAIN — TWO MODES (codified, resolving the WPF `DeferProcessing` drift):**
>   - **`!AllowsCrossThreadChanges` (default) — DRAIN WHAT YOU FILL, synchronously.** Changes are processed
>     SYNCHRONOUSLY in a single affinity-thread pass (S037/S041/S143): the fill and the drain are the same
>     call (`PostChange` sync branch, `CollectionView.cs:1888-1893`). If the synchronous drain exceeds the
>     WPF `DataBindEngine.CrossThreadThreshold` time budget, the overflow is re-queued (WPF
>     `ProcessChangeLog` `mustDeferProcessing`, `CollectionView.cs:1846`) and **deferred to a later drain pass,
>    to be harvested by the app's pump when it next calls the drain API** — it is still drained-what-it-filled,
>    just across a pump boundary. **No deque, no lock.**
>   - **`AllowsCrossThreadChanges` (opt-in) — BUDGET-DRAIN WITH RE-QUEUE.** Producers fill the filling deque;
>     the fill→drain swap (under the mutex) isolates a draining deque; `ProcessChangeLog` drains it on the
>     time budget; **overflow is re-queued back onto the filling deque (WPF `DeferProcessing`,
>     `CollectionView.cs:1804-1830,1850`) for a later harvest** — the drain is NOT self-kicked in-library.
>     Two deques, one swap mutex, one app-pumped budget-drain.
>   - **NO WORK IS EVER DEFERRED TO 11z.** 11n-4 OWNS the drain code (`ProcessChangeLog`'s budgeted drain +
>     `DeferProcessing`'s re-queue) — VAML library code resident in 11n-4. **11z SUPPORTS the dual mode only via
>     API**: the app-side harvest point (S543_1 inbound seam, S540 `IUiExecutor` seam) the APP calls to pull
>     ONE drain pass and harvest the deferred work. That is the REVERSE of 11z mode-1's "our pump harvests the
>     app's async": here the APP's pump (or the 11z-hosted pump) calls OUR drain API, and in-library 11n-4 code
>     runs. WPF's internal Dispatcher self-kick (`_engine.Marshal`) is swapped for this external app-pulled
>     harvest — the collection-view drain is 11n-4's job, the app-side harvest API surface is 11z's, kept
>     distinct to avoid the 11n/11z collision.
> - **ADR-018 verdict — renegotiated:** single-threaded UI paths (default) have ZERO locks; the ONE permitted
>   lock is the opt-in fill→drain swap mutex, exactly where WPF itself locks. `DeferProcessing`/the budgeted
>   drain adds NO new lock. Cross-thread background updates are a STRUCTURED HANDOFF onto the affinity thread
>   — never direct collection mutation. S543_1 (11z) + the S211 lock-free postbox precedent stand as the
>   related seams.
Test `BindingBase_s11n4_test.cpp` (reactive: mutate the ObservableCollection -> the bound ItemsControl
reflects the change live).

> **11n-4 MAIN SURFACE — DELIVERED (both CI lanes GREEN).** Built per DECISION-2 (ADR-018 renegotiated,
> human-gated): the reactive spine's main surface is REAL and permanent (ZERO MINIMAL REAL):
>   - `INotifyPropertyChanged` (formal interface; `ObservableObject` derives from it — DAG anchor flips DONE).
>   - `DispatcherObject` (affinity-thread base: check_access/verify_affinity, PURE READ, zero locks).
>   - `ICollectionView` + `CollectionView : DispatcherObject, ICollectionView, INotifyPropertyChanged,
>     IWeakEventListener` — the live collection read model (Count/Contains/GetItemAt/IndexOf + current-item
>     navigation + Refresh), subscribed to the source WEAKLY (weak_ptr trampoline, weak-lifetime contract).
>   - DECISION-2 change-log/drain OWned IN-LIBRARY here (NO work deferred to 11z): two deques (filling_/
>     draining_), default `!AllowsCrossThreadChanges` = ZERO locks (fill==drain sync on the affinity
>     thread; CrossThreadChangeRejected = the WPF NotSupportedException boundary throw-guard), opt-in
>     `AllowsCrossThreadChanges` = ONE permitted fill->drain swap mutex (WPF _changeLogLock; draining
>     runs OUTSIDE the lock) + `drain_one_pass()` budget-drain with re-queue (the app-pulled harvest the
>     11z seam calls).
>   - `ItemsControl` — incremental per-item container add/remove on CollectionChanged (event-subscription,
>     NOT polled), detach-on-destroy (S245).
>   - Tests: `BindingBase_s11n4_test.cpp` RETAINS the recipes + ADDS the reactive-live section (mutate the

> PREMULTIPLIED final surface for OS compositing); (5) the OS window is created OPAQUE (no
> `GLFW_TRANSPARENT_FRAMEBUFFER` / `GLFW_ALPHA_BITS` / `WS_EX_LAYERED`). This sprint closes all five —

> **WPF-SOURCE-VALIDATED MECHANISM (scan of `dotnet/wpf`, recorded this step — the authoritative model
> VAML mirrors, NOT "handle the special cases differently"):** WPF itself handles **100% of transparency**
> natively on every visual that participates in the render tree — Window chrome, panel `Background`,
> per-element `Opacity`, alpha brushes. The ONLY WPF conditions not handled by WPF's own render path are a
> narrow set that rely on a **secondary COM object** to complete the transparency (the MIL core
> component `milcore.dll` — `DUCE.Channel` / `CompositionTarget.UpdateWindowSettings`), and the contract is
> that **VAML handles 100% of the transparency WPF exposes, composited through the SAME pipeline to Vulkan,
> exactly like any other XAML → Vulkan render surface** — we do NOT defer, special-case, or sidestep that
> secondary-COM step. The mechanism (read from the real source): `Window.cs` `AllowsTransparency` (plain
> DP, default false) → `CreateHwndSourceParameters.UsesPerPixelOpacity` → **`HwndSource.cs` sets
> `WS_EX_LAYERED` + `HwndTarget.BackgroundColor = Colors.Transparent` (clear = alpha 0)** →
> `HwndTarget.cs` builds `MILTransparencyFlags` (`_usesPerPixelOpacity` ORs in **`PerPixelAlpha`**) and
> selects **`MILWindowLayerType.ApplicationManagedLayer`** (per-pixel, what VAML wants) vs
> `SystemManagedLayer` (constant-alpha color-key fallback — which VAML will NOT use as a crutch). The
> "narrow conditions" are ONLY the OS-compositor capability gates `IsOSWindows8OrNewer` /
> `PlatformSupportsTransparentChildWindows` (HwndSourceParameters.cs) — gates on whether the compositor
> can deliver an application-managed layered sprite, i.e. exactly the honest capability result the S590
> composite-alpha probe records per machine, NEVER a reason to degrade the pipeline. VAML therefore
> mirrors the full model: `WS_EX_LAYERED` + `GLFW_TRANSPARENT_FRAMEBUFFER`/`GLFW_ALPHA_BITS 8` (S594),
> transparent clear alpha 0 (S592), premultiplied final surface (S591), and per-element alpha preservation
> (S593) — with no color-key shortcut and no constant-alpha fallback.
> VIEWER GROWTH (anti-grave-whistle): this sprint's token is **S595** (a SplashWindow-shaped transparent
> doc renders live — see-through where transparent, layered where opaque) — no token, no ✅ per the S11+
> OPEN-ENDED clause. ADR-018: ZERO new locks (single-threaded affinity render, the S211 lock-free postbox
> precedent). ADR-011 held: transparency is core DATA (Windows Background/AllowsTransparency + element

## Sprint 11r — UI-compliance test QUEUE (one DEDICATED tester project/exe; each step = ONE UI-affecting surface, flattened one-per-step; each step ends with CONFIRMED content shown on the UI)  [token S640+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (a direct corrective to the Sprint-11 outcome — written into the roadmap, not a
> silent apology):** the recurring failure across 20+ gap sprints was that UI work kept landing with NO visible
> proof — "text isn't on the screen", "splash renders black", "vector logo doesn't draw". That is the exact
> mistake identified at the very first roadmap conversation ("you argued waiting until sprint 11 to see
> anything on the screen") and it recurred. Sprint 11r ends that pattern structurally: from this sprint
> forward, EVERY step that touches the UI MUST end with **confirmed content actually shown on the UI**,
> verified by a **UI-compliance scanner** — not by "it builds and ctest is green". This is the
> `ALWAYS-SEE-IT-ON-SCREEN` contract, baked in.
>
> **A DEDICATED TESTER PROJECT / EXE (driver Q — the answer is YES).** The run → scan → compare loop is NOT
> bolted onto the viewer and NOT a unit-test exe. It is its OWN long-lived project — `vaml_ui_tester/`
> (Windows `vaml_ui_tester.vcxproj` + `vaml_ui_tester-linux/` CMake, mirroring the viewer's structure) — a
> dedicated executable whose ONLY job is: take an authored `.xaml` argument, render it through the REAL
> retained render path (offscreen/windowed), SCAN the rendered UI for compliance, COMPARE to the expected
> outcome declared in that `.xaml`, and exit 0=PASS / 1=FAIL / 2=SKIP (the standalone process boundary a
> script drives, exactly like the S177/S446 real-WSI gates). It consumes ONLY the public surface (ADR-021).
> It is the driver's stated "one app with many xaml files, or a script at input to load and confirm what is
> expected" — the script is a thin loop over `vaml_ui_tester <file.xaml>` per queued file.
>
> **THE SCANNER (the novel, central mechanism — the "how do we know the UI is right?" answer).** Unit tests
> cannot prove pixels the way a display does. Sprint 11r introduces a **reproducible void that the UI must
> fill**: a scanner that (a) renders the authored `.xaml` through the REAL retained render path (offscreen /
> windowed), (b) **scrapes the rendered UI for compliance** against the desired outcome declared in the same
> `.xaml` (coordinates + pixel information / element presence / draw-item counts + positions), and (c)
> **compares to the expected** result, PASS/FAIL. Per the driver's standing guidance: "you must include a
> scanner capability to scrape the UI for information that is compliant. the outcome file could be
> coordinates with pixel information." Where a **pixel-exact PNG comparison** is achievable at high enough
> fidelity, that is one authoritative path (S.Deferred-PNG); otherwise the scanner scrapes structured
> compliance data (draw items, element rects, colors). The driver picked the scan approach as the
> authoritative one and explicitly authorized flexible comparison ("you do you best. we can always change it
> later."). The scanner lives in the dedicated tester project (S641), NOT the viewer.
>
> **SPRINT MECHANISM (KNOWN-KNOWN, deterministic — the reverse of 11q).** This is NOT 11q's "adjust to
> unknown bindings in unknown contexts"; 11r is **known bindings to known types**, deterministic. The tester
> renders N authored `.xaml` files (one per queued surface); the script loads each via the tester, scans,
> compares to the declared outcome, and reports per-step PASS/FAIL. Each step ships THREE things: (1) an
> authored `.xaml` that ALSO declares its expected outcome, (2) the component/surface it exercises, (3) the
> scanner assertion that proves the content is actually on the UI. Every step ends **green on both CI lanes
> AND the content confirmed on-screen via the scanner** (the anti-grave-whistle / anti-black-screen gate).
>
> **ONE CONTROL = ONE STEP (the corrected structure — flattened, NOT bundled).** The prior draft BUNDLED
> several controls per step (S644–S651 as groups) — that is rejected. This sprint is **one UI-affecting
> surface per step**, the authoritative WPF-real control set (Element.h / the 11k-7 audit), ordered
> base-building-block → higher-level exactly as the driver ordered. If there are N surfaces, there are N+
> authored `.xaml` files / N+ steps. The list is NOT limited to controls (driver directive): panels, brushes,
> shapes, text glyphs, AND the recently-added adorner + StickyNote surfaces each get their own step.
>
> **GOVERNING RULES (codified, like 11k's fidelity contract):**
> - **ALWAYS-SEE-IT-ON-SCREEN:** a step that touches a renderable surface is NOT DONE until the content is
>   CONFIRMED on the UI (scanner PASS + both CI lanes green). No token, no ✅, no black-screen, no "it
>   builds" as a substitute for on-screen proof.
> - **DEDICATED TESTER:** the run → scan → compare loop lives in `vaml_ui_tester/` (its own exe), NEVER an
>   afterthought bolted onto the viewer or a unit test.
> - **KNOWN-KNOWN (not 11q):** bindings are KNOWN property paths to KNOWN VM types — no seed-guessing, no
>   placeholder text. The data context is a real, typed VM; the binding is two-way where WPF is two-way.
> - **THE SCANNER IS THE ORACLE:** the `.xaml` declares its expected outcome; the scanner scraps + compares;
>   a mismatch is a FAIL with a structured report (coordinate + pixel detail), never a silent accept.
> - **RENDER-SURFACE CONFORMANCE:** any step that introduces/changes a renderable surface updates
>   `docs/RENDER_SURFACE.md` + re-runs the validator at that step (never silent, NO-GAP).
> - **ZERO new locks (ADR-018), ZERO MINIMAL REAL, ZERO invented names** (all WPF-real per the 11k-7 audit).
>
> **VIEWER GROWTH (anti-grave-whistle):** this sprint's growth is intrinsic — every step's scanner CONFIRMS
> content in the live/retained render path (the tester's offscreen reproduction shares the S212
> `encode_visual_slice` code path with the viewer's generic renderer). No token = no ✅.
> STATUS: **ONGOING** — S640 (Image + Source) DONE first (the driver's #1, 11r-FIRST), S641 the scanner DONE,

>     quad PER DECLARED quad (Name/Kind/Capability/Tolerance from the declaration; X/Y/W/H from the real
>     layout position of the named WPF element). `QuadKind::Border` NOT needed (Border falls under the tight
>     `solid` diff kind — ZERO catalogue churn). Authoring gate confirms the round-trip: `S643-SIDECAR-OK
>     quads=7 catalogued=5 solidsentinels=2`.
>     **DRIVER DESIGN (driver-directed revision of the S643 harness; APPROVED — supersedes the `.cmd`
>     shortcut):** the run/compare harness is NOT a sequence of hard-coded `.cmd` `dotnet run` steps — it is a
>     proper **desktop two-program driver**, a real unit-test process composed of two apps + one looping
>     driver: (A) the **WPF composer** reads `\*.xaml` + args, renders, and writes the **frame (`.bgra`) +
>     metadata (`.json`)**; (B) the **vaml compare** reads the frame + metadata + the declared predicates and
>     performs the **actual UI test against those predicates**, running ALL cases (never short-circuiting on a
>     failure), accumulating ONE aggregated error report (a silent fail is banned — NO-LAZY-LLM). The driver
>     reads a **manifest of test names (one file per test, not per step; ordered as the user wants, e.g. step
>     order)**, and for each test in that order: run A only when the frame+metadata are **missing or stale**,
>     run **B always**, clearing the single render canvas before each A. Memory/VRAM is bounded to **ONE
>     frame at a time** (a single reused canvas) — never N tests composited into one large frame (that would
>     require 16 GiB VRAM and is REJECTED for portability). **Hash scheme (approved):** the metadata `.json`
>     itself carries the `input_hash`; `--rebuild` is provided but NOT the correctness mechanism. The hash is
>     computed over the **PRINCIPLE FILES read in and appended** — the test's `.xaml` source + the committed
>     `tools/capability_catalogue.json` + the `wpf_emitter/*.cs` sources + the `src/presentation/src/scan/*`
>     scanner sources — NOT the rebuilt executable (rebuilding WPF always churns binary bytes), and NOT a
>     hand-bumped version constant (a forgotten bump = a silent stale frame). At WPF's current stage, CHANGING
>     THE SOURCE is all that matters: any edit to the emitter/scanner source forces a re-render (expected +
>     actual) and a full compare; a no-op rebuild reuses the cached frame. `--rebuild` + deleting a file remain
>     manual override escape-hatches. **ACCEPTANCE (recodified):** a step is done when the headless CI lanes
>     are green AND the **desktop two-app test run is green against the real GPU frame** — the desktop test run
>     is REQUIRED for acceptance on this machine (it is precisely how, as the vaml lib → viewer → tester
>     changes, this test run tells us when we break things). CI does NOT run the GPU apps (no GPU on CI), but
>     desktop acceptance DOES include them. **IMPLEMENTATION STATUS: DONE + GREEN** — the approved DRIVER is
>     implemented: `build/run_compare.cmd` (the two-app loop: A-if-stale, B-always, accumulate, one frame at a
>     time over `build/compare_tests.manifest`), `tools/compare_hash.py` (the source-hash authority), the hash
>     embedded in the metadata (`wpf_emitter/HashInput.cs` + `EmitterMetadata.InputHash`), and the tester (B,
>     `vaml_ui_tester.exe`) built via msbuild so B RUNS against the real frame. The drive-clean gate
>     `build/verify_s643.cmd` now runs the driver in its desktop lane (enforced, not skipped) and exits GREEN:
>     `S643 GREEN (both CI lanes + authoring gate + desktop two-app driver)`. NO-GAP: any step that changes
>     the emitter/scanner/compare behavior must commit the source affecting the hash IN THE SAME STEP (the hash
>     is source-derived, so a committed source change IS the invalidation — no separate revision to remember).
>     **OWNER DECISION (accepted):** because an int/bool/string bound slot RENDERS AS A TEXT GLYPH, the five
>     catalogue quads (int01/bool01/str01/text01/icon01) are ALL fuzzy-pool — so the smoke adds TWO no-text
>     geometry sentinels (a `Rectangle` `box01` + a `Border` `border01`) as the ONLY EXACT fails-loud compare
>     path in this step (the loop must be proven CAPABLE of issuing a FAIL on geometry — never a silent
>     all-presence pass). The fuzzy text/icon quads compare on a DECLARED presence floor ("non-empty ==
>     non-empty"), with 0.08 as a SMOKE-ONLY soft start (NEVER a catalogue default or limit). NO-GAP: S644
>     (TextBlock), S656 (Icon), S657 (Label) MUST tighten the fuzzy-compare quality (readable-glyph,
>     auto-locate, tighter band); the geometry sentinels prove the scan→compare loop can FAIL LOUDLY.

      NO-GAP: `Foreground="#RRGGBB"` (and `Background`/`Fill`/`Stroke`/`BorderBrush` on BrushId DPs)
      parse + render in vaml_viewer.** The current readers (S2 `VamlReader::convertLiteral` + S7
      `VBamlReader::convertLiterals`) have **no BrushId arm** (only Int32/Bool/Color/Thickness/Double/
      GridLength), so a `#RRGGBB` literal on a BrushId DP hits `typeName.empty()` → throws UnknownType.
      **Ground truth: WPF's BrushConverter (PresentationCore, Generated) → `Brush.Parse` → `Parsers`.
      `ParseBrush` is a PURE TYPE-LEVEL converter, context-free** (verified in E:\GitRepos\wpf): it does
      NOT register a brush id, holds no shared id registry, no element scoping, no dedup map, no collision
      concern — it just `new SolidColorBrush(ParseHexColor(...))` each time. Non-obvious facts surfaced by
      reading the WPF source: (1) `ParseHexColor` accepts `#RRGGBB`/`#AARRGGBB`/`#ARGB`/`#RGB` with a
      **high-alpha-alpha-first** convention (9→AARRGGBB, 5→ARGB single-digit alpha-first), and the
      5/4-digit single-digit forms alpha-first — so S602's parse_color fix for #RGB/#ARGB is the
      building block; (2) the conversion is pure, no registry — VAML's only adaptation is that it must
      register the fresh SolidColorBrush under `Brush:<id>` on the TARGET ELEMENT so the render-time
      `find_for_element` three-scope walk resolves it (VAML holds a BrushId int, WPF holds the brush
      object — the required divergence is the id-registration, NOT any id-dedup/id-collision machinery
      the earlier plan invented; WPF has none). **Change:** (1) a shared `convert_brush_id_literal`
      helper, the `Parsers.ParseBrush` analogue, added to BOTH readers (S288 parity): parse-as-int →
      `Value::BrushId(id)` (the existing GeometryDrawing numeric convention, unchanged); else
      `parse_color(literal)` succeeds → allocate an owned `SolidColorBrush`, register it under
      `Brush:<id>` on the target element's resources set, return `Value::BrushId(newId)`; else →
      structured `MalformedValue` (WPF throws FormatException; never silent); (2) registration at the
      BUILD CALL SITES (convertLiteral still has no element — WPF's converter is context-free, VAML
      needs the element to register, same as 11k-4's original scoping constraint), owned brush kept in a
      reader-held per-Load `owned_brushes_` vector (like `owned_merged_`), auto-ids from a high base
      offset so they never collide with app-registered small ids (a one-line guard, not a dedup-map
      design — WPF's fresh-object-per-conversion is honored, a color used on multiple elements is a
      separate brush per element, exactly like WPF); (3) end-to-end headless test (both CI lanes):
      `TextBlock Foreground="#FFE8E8E8"` + `Rectangle Fill="Red"` + `Border Background="#80RRGGBB"`

> Each step: authored `.xaml` (declaring its expected outcome) + the surface's component + the scanner
> assertion proving the content is on the UI; both CI lanes green + scanner/on-screen CONFIRMED. The set is
> the WPF-real control surface (Element.h, 11k-7 audit) — panels, brushes, shapes, text glyphs, input,
> selection/container, and the recently-added adorner + StickyNote surfaces, exactly as the driver ordered.

## Sprint 11s — DRIFT ZERO: property identity keyed on (name, ownerType)  (goal: remove the name-only DP-uniqueness drift — VAML uniques/resolves on the WPF ground-truth composite `(name, ownerType)` pair — and un-revert every workaround that drift forced)  [token S800+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the audit verdict of the S033/S036 conversation, ratified here):**
> VAML's property registry uniques + resolves DPs by **NAME alone**, described as "WPF-style". The actual WPF source
> (`E:\GitRepos\wpf`, `DependencyProperty.cs`) uniques + resolves on the composite **`(name, ownerType)`** pair:
> `FromNameKey key = new(name, ownerType)` (src line 251), `PropertyFromName.ContainsKey(key)` → throw on a
> re-registered pair (254-256), `PropertyFromName[key] = dp` (297), lookup by the pair (1018-1038, 959-975).
> **Fidelity to WPF is the product promise and a binding contract** (the standing directive), not a nice-to-have: VAML
> exists to convert commercial C#/WPF apps 1:1 and mechanically into C++. A real WPF app CAN and DOES register
> same-name/different-owner DPs that coexist as distinct objects (`Button.Width` vs `Panel.Width`; `Slider.Delay` vs
> `RepeatButton.Delay`; `Popup.AllowsTransparency` vs `Window.AllowsTransparency`; `Image.StretchDirection` vs
> `Viewbox.StretchDirection`; `TextBlock.FontSize` vs `Control.FontSize`). Name-only uniqueness means the FIRST such
> collision hoses the conversion — the author must manually disambiguate names (global-search-and-replace without name
> resolution) that WPF never required them to disambiguate. That is a functional conversion blocker, not recorded debt.
>
> **THE EVIDENCE THE DRIFT ALREADY COST US (the workaround history this sprint abolishes):** the name-only contract is
> the direct cause of a whole class of prior migration churn that WPF would never have forced:
> - **11j-5** hoisted `Padding`/`HorizontalContentAlignment`/`VerticalContentAlignment`/`FontSize`/`FontFamily` under a
>   single owner `"Control"` **and migrated away** Text's bare `"FontSize"`, Label's dotted `"Label.FontSize"`/
>   `"Label.FontFamily"`/`"Label.HorizontalContentAlignment"`, and Border's dotted `"Border.Padding"` — a migration that
>   is **unnecessary** under `(name, owner)`, where `TextBlock.FontSize`/`Control.FontSize`/`Label.FontSize`/`Border.Padding`
>   all correctly coexist.
> - **11k-9** deliberately **dropped** bare names because they would collide (`Delay`/`Interval` under Slider vs
>   RepeatButton; `AllowsTransparency` under Popup vs Window; `StretchDirection` under Image vs Viewbox) — each documented
>   "NOT silent", but each is a **real WPF DP VAML refuses**. Under `(name, owner)` these are legal and must be **re-added**.
> - **11k-1/11k-8** flagged `TextBlock` has its OWN `Padding` + Font* family (FrameworkElement branch, NOT the Control
>   bundle) — in WPF those are distinct DPs from `Control.FontSize`; under name-only VAML they had to resolve against
>   the shared Control DP.
> These are not "expensive reverts to preserve" — they are **the tax the drift itself collects**. This sprint's refactor
> **abolishes the charge**. The un-revert IS the payoff, not the price.
>
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint, per the audit):** commit to **composite identity `(name, owner)`**.
> The runtime-hierarchy alternative (resolve by an object's class ancestry) is **REJECTED** because it is genuinely
> ambiguous for same-name/different-owner pairs with no shared declaring base (`Slider.Delay` vs `RepeatButton.Delay`) —
> it would reintroduce the hosing. Consequence: `PropertyId` becomes a composite `(name_view, owner_view)` constexpr-safe
> name-token (pair-keyed `==`/`!=`/`std::hash`, still `of()/name()/owner()/valid()`), and EVERY consumer re-keys. The
> **dotted `owner.name` form becomes CANONICAL first-class authoring** (currently `VamlReader` flattens `"Label.Content"`
> into a bare literal name — under this sprint dotted keys resolve as native `(name, owner)` composite lookup).
>
> **REGISTRY CONTRACT AFTER (WPF-faithful):** `DependencyProperty::Register`/`PropertyRegistry::register_key` unique on
> the **`(name, ownerType)` pair** and throw `PropertyAlreadyRegistered` ONLY when the SAME pair is re-registered;
> same-name/different-owner DPs **coexist as distinct DPs**. `try_find/find/id_of/try_id` resolve on the pair.
> The name-only flags (`name`-dedupe, name-unique global DP discipline S095/S09x) are removed.
>
> **VIEWER GROWTH (anti-grave-whistle):** this sprint introduces no NEW renderable control chrome — it re-keys the
> property identity underneath. Its growth token is **S804** (three same-name/different-owner DPs authored + resolved +
> rendered in the LIVE viewer — the coexistence proof on screen; S222_1 RELOAD re-demonstrated). No token, no ✅ per the
> S11+ OPEN-ENDED clause. ADR-018: ZERO new locks (single-threaded registration/resolution, unchanged). ADR-011 held:
> identity is core DATA; the render path is untouched by the re-key (classify/material unchanged).
>
> **RE-VERIFY EVERY PRECEDENT (the S167_1 corrective-token discipline):** this sprint lands as a corrective that
> SUPERSEDES the name-only workarounds IN PLACE — history preserved un-edited, never renumbered to hide the drift; the
> affected prior tokens (11j-5, 11k-9, S095/S09x name-unique DPs, 11k-1 TextBlock-FontSize note) are each marked
> `SUPERSEDED BY 11s` with the coexistence re-adding the same-name DPs they dropped. NO silent backfill; NO invented names.

## Sprint 11t — DP VALUE PIPELINE + THREAD-AFFINITY FIDELITY (fix the S035/S036/S037 drift: WPF pipeline-order + WPF wrong-thread disposition)  (goal: the `DependencyObject` value pipeline runs the WPF order, and wrong-thread DP access throws as WPF `VerifyAccess` does — the implicit cross-thread queue is removed; the change-log is NOT a DP feature)  [token S810+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S036 fidelity audit + the thread-model comparison):** the S036/S037 `DependencyObject` drifted from the real WPF source on two observable axes. **D1 — pipeline order:** S036/S037 run `coerce → validate(coerced)`; WPF runs **`validate(raw) → coerce → validate(coerced)`** (`DependencyObject.cs:653` raw `IsValidValue` on entry, `:1692` re-check after coercion). A raw value that is invalid but happens to coerce to something valid is REJECTED by WPF at the boundary but ACCEPTED by VAML. **D2 — wrong-thread disposition:** S037 auto-QUEUES a wrong-thread write (`SetResult::QUEUED`, drain-on-affinity). WPF has NO such mechanism at the DP layer — `DependencyObject : DispatcherObject` (`DependencyObject.cs:41`) throws `InvalidOperationException` from `VerifyAccess()` on any foreign-thread access (DO.cs:161/412/…), and cross-thread marshalling is the caller's EXPLICIT `Dispatcher.Invoke`/`InvokeAsync`. S037's auto-queue was a non-WPF framework-implicit marshalling channel, and it silently pre-empts the explicit executor seam 11z is built to be. The change-log pattern S037 "generalized onto the notification axis" is a **data-binding / collection-view feature (11n-4's `CollectionView`, opt-in `AllowsCrossThreadChanges`, `CollectionView.cs:1878–1929`)**, never a DP-value queue. This sprint removes the implicit queue, throws, fixes the pipeline order, and records the split so no future sprint re-imports a DP-value queue. **D3 — invented DP change-notification pipeline:** the S041 layer built on S037's queue (the per-thread `ChangeQueue`, the `ChangeProcessor`/`ChangeRecorder` drain-in-registration-order + coalescing, and the `DependencyObject` per-object `add_property_changed` subscriber registry + `ProcessNotificationQueue` + `fire_self_subscribers` + descendant-push postbox) has **no WPF counterpart whatsoever** — WPF notifies ONE `PropertyMetadata.PropertyChangedCallback(this, e)` synchronously inside `NotifyPropertyChange` (DO.cs:1704, 2022-2039) and walks the internal `DependentList.InvalidateDependents` (DO.cs:1732); there is no public per-object subscriber list and no deferred notification queue at the DP layer. VAML's WPF-faithful primitive — `PropertyMetadata::with_changed`/`ChangedFunc` + `md.notifyChanged` in `Set` (PropertyMetadata.h, DO.cpp) — is already present but was bypassed by the binding, which subscribes through the fabricated `add_property_changed`. So 11t must also DELETE the notification pipeline and re-point the binding onto the synchronous callback, not merely narrow the value queue to "notification-only."
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint):** DP value access = **strict single-thread affinity → THROW** (WPF `DependencyObject`). Marshalling = **explicit, via the 11z `IUiExecutor` (S540) + `S543_1` inbound seam** (the `Dispatcher.Invoke`/`InvokeAsync` analogue) — the "they handle the thread or we handle it" boundary is a PLUMBED SEAM, never an implicit writer-side queue. The affinity marker stays a **single thread-id** because VAML's UI is **strictly single-threaded** (equivalent to WPF's single-Dispatcher-per-object today); it is re-declared as "the thread that owns the pump." The `CollectionView` change-log home is **11n-4**, opt-in, entered via the executor drain — never filled by a wrong-thread DP write. **DP change-notification is the synchronous `PropertyMetadata` callback ONLY** (VAML `with_changed`/`notifyChanged` == WPF `PropertyChangedCallback`, DO.cs:2039), dispatched directly in `Set` — there is **no** `add_property_changed` subscriber registry, **no** per-object `ProcessNotificationQueue`, **no** per-thread `ChangeQueue`, and **no** `ChangeProcessor`/`ChangeRecorder`. The S041 pipeline and its descendant-push postbox are DELETED; `BindingExpression` subscribes onto `with_changed` exactly as WPF bindings attach through the metadata callback + `DependentList`.
> **RELATION TO 11s / 11z:** 11s owns the composite `(name, ownerType)` re-key (S800+, DRIFT ZERO). 11t is independent; it does NOT touch the identity key. 11t REMOVES the implicit queue that 11z was going to "undo," so 11z lands clean on the executor seam. 11n-4's DECISION-2 (ADR-018 renegotiated) already owns the opt-in fill→drain swap mutex for collection events; 11t re-affirms it does NOT extend to DP values.
> **VIEWER GROWTH (anti-grave-whistle):** this sprint introduces no NEW renderable feature (value-pipeline + affinity discipline; no control chrome) — viewer UNCHANGED; S222_1 RELOAD still demonstrated. NO silent backfill; NO invented names; ZERO new locks (ADR-018 — the throw replaces the cross-thread queue, it does not add a lock).

## Sprint 11u — InheritOnly drift closure (S039/S040/S041/S044/S045)  (goal: remove the invented `PropertyFlags::InheritOnly` — the WPF-divergent "local override does NOT contribute" semantic — so effective-value resolution matches the real WPF inheritance contract)  [token S814+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S039 fidelity audit):** the S039 audit against the actual WPF source (`E:\GitRepos\wpf`, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit) found that `PropertyFlags::InheritOnly` is **invented surface with NO WPF counterpart**. The authoritative WPF inheritance surface is `FrameworkPropertyMetadataOptions` (`PresentationFramework\System\Windows\FrameworkPropertyMetadata.cs:15-53`), which declares exactly ONE inheritance flag — **`Inherits = 0x020`** — with **no "inherit-only" / "suppress-local-for-inheritance" option**. `InheritOnly` appears **zero times** across all of `WindowsBase` + `PresentationCore` + `PresentationFramework` (grep-verified). In WPF, an inheriting property ALWAYS honors a local override: `EvaluateEffectiveValue` (DependencyObject.cs:1888) returns the LOCAL value when present, and only defers to `InheritanceParent` (`GetValueEntry`, DependencyObject.cs:240) when there is no local entry. The only WPF mechanism that ever "replaces" an inherited value is the **inverse** of suppress-local — coercion/animation PROMOTING an inherited value into a local (`UpdateResult.InheritedValueOverridden`, DependencyObject.cs:1486) — never suppressing a local in favor of the chain. So `InheritOnly`'s "own local override does NOT contribute" is a **conversion blocker** (a real WPF app can never express it, and a faithful VAML must not manufacture it), not recorded debt.
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint):** **remove `InheritOnly` as invented surface.** The faithful `Inherits` contract is `local ?? inherited-from-parent ?? default` — an inheriting property honors a local override exactly as WPF does. Option B (keep + disclose as a non-WPF extension) and Option C (re-interpret via coercion) were both REJECTED: the former would leave a WPF-divergent flag live in the public surface, and the latter would confuse a local override with the coercion-promotion mechanism that is observably different. No public surface should claim WPF fidelity it cannot deliver.
> **RELATION TO 11s/11t:** 11s owns the composite `(name, ownerType)` re-key; 11t owns the DP value pipeline order + wrong-thread throw. 11u is independent — it collapses the inheritance-disposition axis that S039 introduced and S040/S041/S044 layered onto. It does NOT touch the identity key or the thread-affinity throw.
> **VIEWER GROWTH (anti-grave-whistle):** this sprint introduces no NEW renderable control chrome (a flag-collapse underneath the value pipeline) — viewer UNCHANGED; S222_1 RELOAD still demonstrated. No silent backfill; NO invented names (the flag is being REMOVED, not re-spelled); ZERO new locks (ADR-018 — a flag-collapse is single-threaded registration/resolution).

## Sprint 11aa — FrameworkPropertyMetadataOptions fidelity (close the S045 "all flags honored" drift: represent + honor the real WPF framework-property flag set, minus the `InheritOnly` invented flag that 11u removed; `BindsTwoWayByDefault` gains runtime effect)  [token S818+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S045 fidelity audit):** the S045 "all flags honored" claim was audited against the actual WPF source (`E:\GitRepos\wpf`, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit) and found to hold for only a small subset of the real flag surface. VAML's `PropertyFlags` today is `None`, `Inherits`, `ReadOnly`, `BindsTwoWayByDefault` (carried through metadata but **no runtime behavior**), and `InheritOnly` (invented, removed by 11u). The authoritative WPF surface is `FrameworkPropertyMetadataOptions` (`PresentationFramework\System\Windows\FrameworkPropertyMetadata.cs:18-55`): `None`, `AffectsMeasure=0x001`, `AffectsArrange=0x002`, `AffectsParentMeasure=0x004`, `AffectsParentArrange=0x008`, `AffectsRender=0x010`, `Inherits=0x020`, `OverridesInheritanceBehavior=0x040`, `NotDataBindable=0x080`, `BindsTwoWayByDefault=0x100`, `Journal=0x400`, `SubPropertiesDoNotAffectRender` (+ further arms beyond the audited range). WPF HONORS these in `FrameworkElement.OnPropertyChanged` (`FrameworkElement.cs:2198-2251`): `AffectsParentMeasure/Arrange` → nearest layout-parent `InvalidateMeasure/InvalidateArrange`; `AffectsMeasure` → `InvalidateMeasure`; `AffectsArrange` → `InvalidateArrange`; `AffectsRender` → `InvalidateVisual` (gated by `SubPropertiesDoNotAffectRender`, `FrameworkElement.cs:2251`). Running with only a subset means a faithful VAML CANNOT express a real WPF metadata row (a real WPF control declaring `AffectsMeasure | AffectsRender` has no VAML equivalent) — a **conversion blocker** per Rule 1, not recorded debt.
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint):** **add the missing real flags + honor them.** The faithful contract is that every `FrameworkPropertyMetadataOptions` arm named in the WPF source is represented AND produces its WPF observable effect. No invented flag survives 11u — 11aa adds only flags with a real WPF counterpart (FPM.cs:18-55) and wires each to its honor site (FE.cs:2198-2251). `BindsTwoWayByDefault` moves from "carried-only" to its runtime effect. `Journal`/`SubPropertiesDoNotAffectRender` are represented + carried; their full observable surface is recorded scope (Journal's serialization side is a later concern) — the FLAG is present and its already-true honor arm is wired, not silently dropped.
> **RELATION TO 11s/11t/11u/11z:** 11s owns the composite `(name, ownerType)` re-key; 11t owns pipeline order + wrong-thread throw + the `S810_1`/`S810_2` validation correctives; 11u removed the invented `InheritOnly`. 11aa is independent — it widens the flag surface on the surviving `PropertyFlags` bits (11u left `None`/`Inherits`/`ReadOnly`/`BindsTwoWayByDefault` ordinals unchanged, and 11aa adds new HIGHER bits so the surviving ordinals stay stable). It does NOT touch the identity key, the pipeline order, or the affinity throw. 11z's executor seam consumes the 11aa `Affects*`-driven invalidation in the retained scene.
> **VIEWER GROWTH (anti-grave-whistle):** this sprint DOES move the viewer — `Affects*` invalidation makes layout-affecting DPs (StackPanel/Grid `Width`/`Margin`, TextBlock `Foreground`/`FontSize`) re-layout + re-render through the flags instead of ad-hoc wiring, so the existing controls visibly repaint (NOT new control chrome; the S126/S208 layout axes already exist). S222_1 RELOAD still demonstrated. No silent backfill; NO invented names (only real FPM.cs arms added); ZERO new locks (ADR-018 — flag-driven invalidation is single-threaded Set-time + layout invalidation under the S126 affinity-thread model).

## Sprint 11ab — S120 UIElement-base dep:S097 drift closure (Visibility / Opacity / transform / layout-slot WPF-fidelity)  (goal: the S120 UIElement base's four RENDER/LAYOUT axes match the real WPF source — the S120 audit drift removed)  [token S821+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S120 dep:S097 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit):** the S120 `UIElement` base (derives `DependencyObject`; visibility, opacity, transform owner slot, layout slot) was audited against the actual WPF source (`E:\GitRepos\wpf`, `PresentationCore\System\Windows\UIElement.cs` + `PresentationFramework\System\Windows\FrameworkElement.cs`) and found to drift on ALL FOUR axes — four distinct fidelity defects, each a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must not manufacturing behavior WPF does not have), not recorded debt:
> - **Visibility (minor) — missing boundary validation.** WPF `VisibilityProperty` registers `new ValidateValueCallback(ValidateVisibility)` (`UIElement.cs:2946`) — the DP boundary rejects any value outside `Visible(0)/Hidden(1)/Collapsed(2)`. VAML's `Visibility` is a bare Int32 DP with NO validation, so an authored `Visibility="3"`/`"-1"` is silently accepted. (VAML's Int32-rides-enum is its cross-cutting WPF-enum convention — S648/S600/CONVERTER — and is NOT the drift; the drift is the absent `ValidateValueCallback`.)
> - **Opacity (MATERIAL) — invented Inherits + invented [0,1] validation.** WPF `OpacityProperty` is `DependencyProperty.Register("Opacity", typeof(double), typeof(UIElement), new UIPropertyMetadata(1.0d, changed))` (`UIElement.cs:2660-2665`) with **NO `FrameworkPropertyMetadataOptions.Inherits`** and **NO `ValidateValueCallback`** — grep-verified across `WindowsBase` + `PresentationCore` + `PresentationFramework`. WPF propagates Opacity via the **COMPOSITOR** (`base.VisualOpacity = Opacity`, `UIElement.cs:2689-2691`), NOT DP inheritance, and accepts ANY double. VAML registered Opacity as `PropertyFlags::Inherits` + `with_validate([0,1])` — both invented, observably divergent: a descendant reads an inherited DP value WPF never delivers, and `Opacity="-1"`/`"1.5"`/`NaN` throws/REJECTS where WPF accepts.
> - **RenderTransform — type narrowed + invented finite-validate + missing RenderTransformOrigin.** WPF `RenderTransformProperty` is `typeof(Transform)` (the abstract hierarchy), default `Transform.Identity` (`UIElement.cs:1335-1340`), with authored `RotateTransform`/`ScaleTransform`/`TranslateTransform`/… children and NO `ValidateValueCallback` (any Transform, even a NaN matrix, is accepted). VAML's S208 closure shipped a bare `Matrix2D` DP + an invented `is_transform_valid` NaN/Inf rejection + NO `RenderTransformOrigin` (WPF `UIElement.cs:1378`). A real WPF doc authoring `RenderTransformOrigin` or a `RotateTransform` child cannot express it.
> - **Layout slot — STRUCTURAL divergence.** The layout slot (Margin, HorizontalAlignment, VerticalAlignment, Width, MinWidth/MaxWidth, Height, MinHeight/MaxHeight) lives on **`FrameworkElement`** in WPF (e.g. `WidthProperty` at `FrameworkElement.cs:3463` with `AffectsMeasure` + `IsWidthHeightValid`), NOT on `UIElement`. VAML has NO `FrameworkElement` type — it collapsed the layout slot (and the FE surface) into `UIElement`. Per the 11k ground-truth base-class audit (`TextBlock : FrameworkElement`; Border/Canvas/Grid/StackPanel/DockPanel/WrapPanel/Viewbox/Image/shapes are the FrameworkElement-branch NON-Controls), this is a base-class-placement divergence — the FE DPs are registered on the wrong node.
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint):** close each of the four on the WPF-observable contract. `Visibility` gains the WPF boundary validation; `Opacity` loses `Inherits` + validation and moves to the WPF compositor model (ancestor product at encode time); `RenderTransform` becomes a WPF-faithful `Transform`-object DP (+ `RenderTransformOrigin`, finite-validate moved off the DP boundary); and a real `FrameworkElement : UIElement` base is introduced carrying the layout slot + FE surface, with the FrameworkElement-branch re-based onto it. Each resolves the exact drift, no invented surface is added, and the S208/S122/etc. CLOSURE tokens they superseded are re-pointed in place (the S167_1 corrective-token discipline — history preserved, never renumbered to hide the drift).
> **RELATION TO 11s/11t/11u/11aa/11z:** 11s owns composite `(name, ownerType)` identity; 11t owns the value pipeline order + wrong-thread throw + the `S810_1` validation-disposition (a false `ValidateFunc` THROWS `InvalidPropertyValueException`); 11u removed the invented `InheritOnly`; 11aa added + honored the real `FrameworkPropertyMetadataOptions` flags (the `Affects*` invalidation, FE.cs:2198-2251). 11ab is independent of all of those (no identity-key change, no pipeline-order change, no thread change) — it closes the S120 dep:S097 UIElement-base drift, and it consumes 11aa's S818 `Affects*` invalidation (the layout slot moves onto FrameworkElement with its `Affects*` honor retained). 11z's executor seam is untouched. **NOTE (11u re-verification):** 11u S815's "Opacity (a plain inheriting property) still cascades + pushes" — and the S040/S044/S208 "Opacity is Inherits" citations — are **SUPERSEDED BY 11ab** (Opacity is no longer Inheriting; its subtree alpha is the compositor-model encoder chain). The 11u/11n inheritance suites re-verify against a NON-inheriting Opacity.
> **VIEWER GROWTH (anti-grave-whistle):** this sprint moves the viewer — S825 authors the closed surfaces (`Visibility` boundary, compositor-opacity, `RenderTransformOrigin` + an authored `RotateTransform`, FE-branch alignment/Width/Height) and renders them LIVE (S222_1 RELOAD re-demonstrated). ## Sprint 11ac — S123 Measure-contract semantics drift closure (DesiredSize-bounds / Stretch-pass / Measure-entry WPF-fidelity)  (goal: the S123 measure contract — `Measure(available) → DesiredSize`, stretch-vs-wrap — matches the real WPF source's measure semantics; the S123 audit residual drift removed)  [token S827+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S123 dep:S122 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit):** the S123 measure contract was audited against the actual WPF source (`E:\GitRepos\wpf`, `PresentationCore\System\Windows\UIElement.cs` + `PresentationFramework\System\Windows\FrameworkElement.cs`) and found to drift on the MEASURE SEMANTICS — three distinct fidelity defects, each a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must not manufacture measure behavior WPF does not have):
> - **DesiredSize-bounds (MATERIAL) — eager clamp to the offer.** The S123 `UIElement::Measure` stores `desired_size_ = { max(0, min(d.width, available.width)), max(0, min(d.height, available.height)) }` — an eager clamp to the offered size. WPF **does NOT clamp**: `FrameworkElement.MeasureCore` returns `clippedDesired = desiredSize + margin`, `Math.Max(0, …)` only (FE.cs:4446/4508), and `UIElement.Measure` explicitly documents that the returned DesiredSize **may EXCEED the constraint** (UIElement.cs:541-551); the arrange-side clip is a SEPARATE `NeedsClipBounds` concern (FE.cs:4574-4600). The "measure-to-content, may be bigger than the slot" signal is exactly what lets scroll/content-measure parents (`IStackMeasureScrollData`, `ScrollViewer`) discover they need more room. VAML's `min(d, available)` swallows that signal: a child wanting 1000px offered 300px is measured at 300px and can never report it needs more.
> - **Stretch-pass (MATERIAL) — alignment decided in `Measure`; invented "Stretch + infinite → wrap" branch.** WPF **does NOT consult alignment during `Measure`**: `FrameworkElement.MeasureCore` sets `arrangeSize = available` and measures content + margins only (FE.cs:4358-4411); the Stretch fall-back (`if (HorizontalAlignment != Stretch) arrangeSize = unclippedDesiredSize`, FE.cs:4617-4623) happens in **`ArrangeCore`**, and `MeasureCore` returns content (never "fill" for Stretch). VAML's `compute_measured_desired` folds "Stretch + finite → available (fill)" AND the invented "Stretch + infinite → wraps to content (can't stretch into infinity)" into `Measure` — conflating alignment (an arrange-time enum) with available-bounds (a measure-time input) in a way WPF never does.
> - **Measure-entry (minor) — no reentrancy guard, no clean-element early-out, no `Collapsed` skip.** WPF `UIElement.Measure` reentrancy-guards via `using (Dispatcher.DisableProcessing())` (UIElement.cs:561-563), early-returns when already measured + constraint unchanged (`if (IsMeasureValid && !neverMeasured && isCloseToPreviousMeasure) return;`, UIElement.cs:648-651), and short-circuits a `Visibility.Collapsed` element (skip measure, keep dirty, UIElement.cs:661-676). VAML `UIElement::Measure` re-runs `MeasureOverride` unconditionally and clears `measure_dirty_` with no clean-element early-out, no guard, no Collapsed skip (S126's dirty respect lives in the *panels*, not the element contract).
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint):** close each on the WPF-observable contract. **`Measure`/`MeasureOverride` return content + margin only, NOT clamped to available** (DesiredSize may exceed the offer — the ScrollViewer/measure-to-content signal restored); the **Stretch-vs-wrap fill decision moves OUT of `Measure` and into the arrange/finalize pass only** (reading the S824a-corrected alignment ordinals, `Stretch=3`), and the invented "Stretch + infinite → wrap" branch is DELETED (with Stretch an arrange-only concern, an unbounded axis to a Stretch child yields the child's content size — `MeasureOverride` already returns it, so no "wrap" special-case is needed); and **`Measure` gains the WPF entry spectrum** (reentrancy guard + clean-element-and-same-constraint early-out + `Collapsed` skip). Each resolves the exact drift, no invented surface is added. **Two items the S123 audit surfaced are NOT re-litigated here** — they are already resolved upstream and are recorded as `SUPERSEDED BY`/token-lock, not re-opened: the `float`-at-compositor / `double`-at-DP-surface split is the deliberate **S593** token-lock (ADR-018, deliberate WPF-faithful mirror, NOT drift); and the **MinWidth/MinHeight/MaxWidth/MaxHeight + alignment-ordinal + layout-slot-owner** gap is closed by **Sprint 11ab S824/S824a** (the real `FrameworkElement` base carrying the layout slot + the WPF-true `Left=0,Center=1,Right=2,Stretch=3`/`Top=0,Center=1,Bottom=2,Stretch=3` ordinals + `ValidateValueCallback`). 11ac re-verifies against the post-11ab `FrameworkElement` base; it does NOT re-open those.
> **RELATION TO 11s/11t/11u/11aa/11ab/11z:** 11s owns composite `(name, ownerType)` identity; 11t owns the value pipeline order + wrong-thread throw + the `S810_1` validation-disposition; 11aa added + honored the real `FrameworkPropertyMetadataOptions` flags (the `Affects*` invalidation, FE.cs:2198-2251); 11ab closed the S120 UIElement-base drift (Visibility/Opacity/RenderTransform + the `FrameworkElement` layout-slot relocation + alignment ordinals, S821–S826). 11ac is independent of all of those (no identity-key change, no pipeline-order change, no thread change, no base-ownership move) — it closes the **S123 measure-contract semantics** on the layout math that S824's re-base already re-pointed onto `FrameworkElement`. 11ac consumes 11ab's `FrameworkElement` (the slot DPs live there now) and leaves 11z's executor seam untouched. The corrected alignment ordinals feed the arrange/finalize pass (Stretch=3). S126's panel-level dirty respect is unchanged; 11ac adds the element-level `Measure` entry contract on top.
> **VIEWER GROWTH (anti-grave-whistle):** this sprint moves the viewer — S830 authors the closed surfaces (a child exceeding its offered slot, a Stretch/Fill alignment on BOTH a bounded and an unbounded cross-axis, and a toggled `Visibility="Collapsed"` sibling) and renders them LIVE (S222_1 RELOAD re-demonstrated). No silent backfill; NO invented names (all WPF-real, 11k-7-closed); ZERO new locks (ADR-018 — single-threaded registration + Set-time + encode, the S126 affinity model unchanged).

WPF `UIElement.Measure` explicitly returns a DesiredSize that may EXCEED the constraint (documented twice at `UIElement.cs:541-551`; the arrange-side clip is a SEPARATE `NeedsClipBounds` concern, `FrameworkElement.cs:4574-4600`) — the "measure-to-content, may be bigger than the slot" signal is exactly what lets scroll/content-measure parents (`IStackMeasureScrollData`, `ScrollViewer`) discover they need more room. VAML's `min(d, available)` swallows that signal: a child wanting 1000px offered 300px is measured at 300px and can never report it needs more. VAML's `compute_measured_desired` folds "Stretch + finite → available (fill)" AND the invented "Stretch + infinite → wraps to content (can't stretch into infinity)" into `Measure` — conflating alignment (an arrange-time enum) with available-bounds (a measure-time input) in a way WPF never does. Fix: (1) `Measure`/`MeasureOverride` return **pure content + margin** DesiredSize regardless of alignment (S827's math); (2) the Stretch-vs-wrap fill decision moves into the arrange/finalize pass only (`compute_final_rect`), reading the S824a-corrected alignment ordinals (`Stretch=3`); (3) **DELETE the `compute_measured_desired` stretch/infinite special-case** — with Stretch an arrange-only concern, an infinite cross-axis to a Stretch child simply yields the child's content size (which `MeasureOverride` already returns), so no "wrap" branch is needed.
