## Sprint 11ad — S124 Arrange-contract + clip drift closure (ArrangeCore / child-wins-then-clip / conditional clip / Arrange-entry WPF-fidelity)  (goal: the S124 arrange contract — `Arrange(finalRect) → final_rect` + the render-slot clip — matches the real WPF source's `ArrangeCore`/`Arrange`/`GetLayoutClip` semantics; the S124 audit residual drift removed)  [token S832+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S124 dep:S123 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit):** the S124 arrange contract + clip was audited against the actual WPF source (`E:\GitRepos\wpf`, `PresentationCore\System\Windows\UIElement.cs` + `PresentationFramework\System\Windows\FrameworkElement.cs`) and found to drift on the ARRANGE + CLIP SEMANTICS — three clusters of fidelity defects, each a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must not manufacture arrange/clip behavior WPF does not have):
>
> - **Arrange-squeeze (MATERIAL) — the child-wins-then-clip strategy is INVERTED.** WPF `FrameworkElement.ArrangeCore` explicitly arranges a squeezed child at its **full `unclippedDesiredSize`, NOT a smaller size**, and records `NeedsClipBounds = true` so the renderer clips the overflow later — `arrangeSize = finalRect.Size` start (FE.cs:4539), margin-reduced (FE.cs:4547-4548), then the replace-if-smaller rule at **FE.cs:4595-4606** (`if (DoubleUtil.LessThan(arrangeSize.Width, unclippedDesiredSize.Width)) { NeedsClipBounds = true; arrangeSize.Width = unclippedDesiredSize.Width; }`), the non-Stretch fall-back `arrangeSize = unclippedDesiredSize` (FE.cs:4617-4623), and the clientSize-vs-clippedInkSize clip flag (FE.cs:4681-4687). The arrange contract comment is explicit: *"we will not actually arrange a child at a smaller size … so lets replace the smaller arrange size with UnclippedDesiredSize and then clip the guy later"* (FE.cs:4522-4531). VAML's `compute_final_rect` (LayoutSlot.cpp/h) instead **clamps the child to `min(desired, available)`** (non-Stretch) or `available` (Stretch) — it **shrinks the child to fit the slot, so overflow never exists to clip**. This is the **inverse** of WPF's strategy: WPF keeps the child big + clips; VAML makes the child small so nothing overflows. `clip_to_bounds` (S124) is thereby a near-no-op in the arrange flow (there is no overflow to feed it), and the whole "clip bounds honored by render slot" promise is vacuous.
> - **Clip (MATERIAL) — unconditional vs WPF's conditional `NeedsClipBounds`/`ClipToBounds` gate.** WPF's clip is computed by `ensureClip` at the end of `Arrange` (UIElement.cs:884 → 3056) and `GetLayoutClip` (base UIElement.cs:3322; FrameworkElement.cs:4862), and is applied **only when `NeedsClipBounds` is true or `ClipToBounds` is true** — a fitting element gets `null` (no clip at all). VAML's `clip_to_bounds` (LayoutSlot.cpp:139, LayoutSlot.h) clips **unconditionally** (always intersects), and there is **no `NeedsClipBounds` state machine and no `ClipToBounds` DP**. So the "when" the clip applies is wrong, and the explicit WPF opt-in flag is absent.
> - **Arrange-entry (minor) — no `Arrange` guard spectrum.** WPF `UIElement.Arrange` (a) throws `InvalidOperationException` on an Inf/NaN slot (UIElement.cs:798-809), (b) short-circuits a `Visibility.Collapsed` / layout-suspended element — records `_finalRect` but returns WITHOUT arranging (UIElement.cs:811-828), (c) backfills `Measure` when `MeasureDirty || NeverMeasured` (UIElement.cs:833-862), and (d) calls `ensureClip(finalRect.Size)` at the end (UIElement.cs:884-901). VAML `UIElement::Arrange` (src/core/src/UIElement.cpp) does none of these: an infinite `arrangeSlot` silently produces garbage `final_rect_`; a Collapsed element is arranged normally; a never-measured element is arranged with a stale/zero `desired_size_`; and no clip is applied at arrange (S829 fixes the *Measure* entry only — the arrange-side entry is NOT covered).
>
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint):** close each cluster on the WPF-observable contract. **Arrange keeps the child at its unclipped desired size when the slot squeezes it**, setting a needs-clip flag instead of shrinking the child — restoring WPF's "child wins then clip" so `clip_to_bounds` has real overflow to honor; the **render-slot clip becomes conditional** on that flag (or an explicit `ClipToBounds` DP), matching `NeedsClipBounds`/`GetLayoutClip`; and **`Arrange` gains the WPF entry spectrum** (Inf/NaN guard + Collapsed skip + measure-on-arrange backfill + ensureClip at the end). Each resolves the exact drift, no invented surface is added.
> **DEPENDENCE ON 11ab/11ac (recorded, NOT re-litigated):** 11ad sits **after** 11ac and consumes 11ab's `FrameworkElement : UIElement` base (S824 — the slot + Min/Max/Width/Height land there) and 11ac's measure corrections (S827 DesiredSize-no-longer-clamped-to-offer, so `desired_size()` may EXCEED `available`; S828 Stretch-moves-to-arrange, so `compute_measured_desired` no longer folds alignment). **11ad is the ARRANGE-side seat of those corrections:** with DesiredSize now allowed to exceed the offer (S827) and Stretch decided at arrange (S828), it is `compute_final_rect` (the arrange math) that must now implement the child-wins-then-clip squeeze (FE.cs:4574-4687) + the conditional clip. 11ad does NOT re-open the measure/base decisions.
> **RELATION TO 11s/11t/11u/11aa/11ab/11ac/11z:** 11s owns composite `(name, ownerType)` identity; 11t the value-pipeline order + validation disposition; 11aa the `Affects*` flags; 11ab the UIElement-base drift (Visibility/Opacity/Transform + `FrameworkElement` layout-slot relocation + alignment ordinals, S821–S826); 11ac the measure-contract semantics (S827–S831); 11ad closes the **arrange-contract + clip** on the layout math S824's re-base already re-pointed onto `FrameworkElement`. 11ad is independent of 11s/11t/11u (no identity/pipeline/thread change) and leaves 11z's executor seam untouched. 11ad consumes 11aa's `AffectsArrange`/`AffectsRender` invalidation for any new property (e.g. `ClipToBounds` must carry `AffectsArrange`). ZERO new locks (ADR-018 — single-threaded registration + Set-time + arrange/encode, the S126 affinity model unchanged).
> **VIEWER GROWTH (anti-grave-whistle):** S836 authors the closed surfaces LIVE — a squeezed child in a narrower StackPanel cross-axis that must keep its desired width and clip overflow (S832), a `ClipToBounds="true"` panel whose child is clipped at the slot (S833/S834), and an authored `NaN`/infinite sized element path rejected / a `Visibility="Collapsed"` sibling skipped at arrange (S835) — resolved + rendered via the generic renderer (S222_1 RELOAD re-demonstrated). No silent backfill; NO invented names (all WPF-real, 11k-7-closed); ZERO new locks.

- S832 dep:S831  **ARRANGE-SQUEEZE FIDELITY — child-wins-then-clip: `compute_final_rect` keeps the child at its unclipped desired size and reports needs-clip, instead of shrinking it to fit the slot.** WPF `FrameworkElement.ArrangeCore` (FE.cs:4539-4687) arranges a squeezed child at its **full `unclippedDesiredSize`** and sets `NeedsClipBounds = true` (FE.cs:4595-4606), so the child is never arranged smaller than what its own `MeasureOverride` accepted (FE.cs:4522-4531) — the bigger child is then clipped against the smaller slot. VAML's `compute_final_rect` (LayoutSlot.h/cpp) inverts this: it clamps the non-Stretch child to `min(desired, available)` and the Stretch child to `available`, so `final_rect_` never exceeds the slot and there is no overflow to clip. ## Sprint 11af — S240 PropertyPath grammar drift closure (empty→Direct, /, ^, (), whitespace-in-name)  [token S845+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S240/S242/S244 binding-core audit per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\MS\Internal\Data\PathParser.cs + System\Windows\PropertyPath.cs):** S240's "hand-rolled WPF-faithful grammar" silently dropped operators WPF's parser actually has, and one claim was flatly wrong — the empty-path case. The migration contract (commercial WPF→VAML with zero behavioral change) admits no partial credit, so each is a mandatory close:
> **D1 EMPTY→DIRECT (the flatly-wrong claim).** WPF treats `Path=""` / `Path="."` as a VALID `Direct` self-binding to the whole object — `if (_n == 0) ... return new SourceValueInfo[] { new(Direct, ...) }` (PathParser.cs:83-89) — and a leading `.`/`/`/`[` at State.Init is legal (:103-115). VAML declared empty a Class-A `Empty` error and rejected a leading `.` as `TrailingDot` — the exact opposite of WPF. Direct self-binding (`{Binding}`, no Path) is thereby unconvertible.
> **D2 DRILL-IN OPERATOR — `/` missing.** WPF grammar: each level is `.propname` / `/propname` / `[index]` / `/[index]` (:57-66); `/` = `DrillIn.Always`, `.` = `DrillIn.Never`, first level defaults `IfNeeded` (StartNewLevel resets to `Never`, :127-136/:372). VAML has no `/` at all — `/Items[0]`, `/propname` unconvertible.
> **D3 INDEXER ESCAPE — `^` missing.** WPF `EscapeChar = '^'` escapes `, ( ) ] ^` and whitespace inside indexers (:417, :239-247). VAML's `parse_index_inner` has no escape handling.
> **D4 PAREN STRING + MULTI-PARAM INDEXERS.** WPF indexer is a comma-separated `IndexerParamInfo{parenString, valueString}` list (:17-32, :172-181) with nested `[ [ ] ]`. VAML accepts a single Integer/StringKey only.
> **D5 WHITESPACE-IN-NAME (bonus found in audit).** `IsSpecialChar` is only `.` `/` `[` `]` (:401-405) — a name is read until one of those and `.Trim()`ed (:150-165), so `"First Name"` is a legal property name; internal whitespace is NOT a boundary. VAML's `is_name_break` treats all whitespace as a syntax boundary — WPF-divergent.
>
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint — the contract forces full close):** the VAML parser is rewritten as the WPF Init→DrillIn→Prop(/Indexer) state machine: empty/`.` → a valid `Direct` (moved OUT of Class-A-error into a valid read that returns the root value; `PropertyPathError::Empty` stays as the stable no-error/ok tag), leading `.`/`/`/`[` accepted, `/` reproduced as `DrillIn.Always` (semantics — drill into a collection/items view — rides in with the collection reader per the recorded NO-GAP, parse is faithful now), `^` escape inside indexers, the comma-separated `(paren)value` param list (multi-param `[i,j]` staged with multi-dim arrays; the single-Integer/StringKey convenience forms are preserved), and internal whitespace legal in names. `{Binding}` with an empty path becomes a valid self-binding. **Relation:** dep:S240; independent of S803's composite DP-key migration (the reader resolves a name against the object; the composite owner resolution is S803's concern). ZERO new locks (ADR-018). ZERO invented names. Supersedes the pre-11af "Empty = Class-A error" S240_1/BindingDiagnostic precondition — recorded, history preserved un-edited.
> **VIEWER GROWTH (anti-grave-whistle):** S849 authors the closed surface LIVE in the viewer (S222_1 RELOAD re-demonstrated) — a `{Binding}` with no Path binds the whole DataContext; a collection path resolves through `/`; a property named with an embedded space / a paren key resolves — with the WPF-faithful observable each implies. No token, no ✅ per the S11+ OPEN-ENDED clause. No silent backfill; NO invented names (all WPF-real); ZERO new locks.

- S845 dep:S240  **GRAMMAR STATE-MACHINE REWRITE (D1+D2+D5): WPF-faithful path parser.** Rewrite the parse core as the WPF Init→DrillIn→Prop(/Indexer) loop (PathParser.cs state machine); empty/`.` → valid `Direct` (is_direct()); leading `.`/`/`/`[` accepted at State.Init (:103-115); `/` → `DrillIn.Always`, `.` → `DrillIn.Never`, first level `IfNeeded`, per-level reset to `Never` (StartNewLevel :372); names read until `.`/`/`/`[`/`]` honoring paren-level, then trimmed (internal whitespace legal — D5). `Empty` is retired as a syntax error (kept as the stable no-error/ok tag); Class-A errors are the real remaining arms (UnterminatedIndexer, EmptyIndexer, MalformedIndex, UnclosedQuote, UnmatchedParen). Preserve the existing single-Integer/single-StringKey convenience accessors (backward compatible). `[i,j]` multi-param staged with multi-dim arrays as a recorded NOT-CLOSED (per Rule 1, explicit, not silent). > - **(a) The DataTrigger code-vs-test CONTRADICTION (the flatly-wrong claim in the DONE note).** `StyleApplier.cpp` hard-gates the DataTrigger branch to `fires = false` — *"Until a DataTrigger read supplies a real owning object type, Data triggers never fire"* — yet `StyleApply_test.cpp`'s LAST test asserts the DataTrigger FIRES (applied==1, OUT==420) and the S363 DONE note claims "DataTrigger on S240-path match through the dependency-object reader". WPF subscribes continuously (`StyleHelper` `OnTriggerSourcePropertyInvalidated`, `AddPropertyTriggerWithAction`) and un-fires when the trigger condition leaves the match. This is a **documented-but-not-delivered** behavior — a real conversion blocker (a WPF trigger that re-fires on a data change has no VAML equivalent).

> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S364 dep:S363 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against
> `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\{VisualState,VisualStateGroup,VisualStateManager,ControlTemplate,FrameworkTemplate}.cs`):**
> the S364 `[DONE]` marker overstates fidelity on FIVE observable axes — the exact findings of the S364 audit recorded at the sprint head. Each is a conversion blocker
> (a faithful VAML must not manufacture a state mechanism WPF does not have), not recorded debt:
> - **D1 — the state mechanism itself is INVENTED.** WPF's `VisualState` is a thin **Storyboard-based** class: `[ContentProperty("Storyboard")] public class VisualState : DependencyObject { public string Name { get; set; } public Storyboard Storyboard { get; set; } }` (`VisualState.cs`) — the ENTIRE effect of a state is its `Storyboard` (animated property values). VAML's `VisualState{name; brushProperty; owned SolidColorBrush; engaged}` + a bespoke `enter_state/exit_state/find_state` engine has NO WPF counterpart.
> - **D2 — grouping + transition are missing.** WPF groups states under `VisualStateGroup` (mutually-exclusive `States` + `Transitions` + `CurrentState` + change events) on an ATTACHED `VisualStateManager.VisualStateGroups` DP of a `stateGroupsRoot` FrameworkElement (`VisualStateGroup.cs`), and drives them through `VisualStateManager.GoToState(control, stateName, useTransitions)` (`VisualStateManager.cs`), which resolves a `VisualTransition`, generates dynamic transition Storyboards, and raises the state-changed events. VAML has no Group, no GoToState, no transitions, no attached `VisualStateGroups`.
> - **D3 — `exit_state` does not revert.** `exit_state` re-writes the SAME color and the test asserts red is STILL present after exit — WPF returns the property to its pre-state value on leaving a state (via storyboard handoff/removal). Observable bug, not just "unlike WPF".
> - **D4 — precedence.** `enter_state` does `control.Set(...)` = a LOCAL (band `Local=11`) that outranks style/animation; WPF state effects are animations/trigger-setters (`EffectiveValueEntry.cs:613-620` — lower bands).
> - **D5 — `ControlTemplate` target-type + TemplateBinding.** `ControlTemplate.cs`: `ValidateTargetType` (target must be assignable to `Control`/`Page`/`PageFunctionBase`, default `DefaultTargetType = typeof(Control)`), `ValidateTemplatedParent` (throws on unassociated templates), and `{TemplateBinding}` becomes a real `Binding { OneWay, RelativeSource=TemplatedParent }` pushed on change notification — VAML validates NO target type and `apply_control_template`'s TemplateBinding read DISCARDS the value (`const Value v = control.Get(...); (void)v;`).
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint — the contract forces full close, no scoped option):** (1) the VISUAL-STATE mechanism is re-based on the REAL WPF `VisualState` (`VisualState + Storyboard`), `VisualStateGroup` (mutually-exclusive `States` + `Transitions` + `CurrentState`), and `VisualStateManager.GoToState(control, stateName, useTransitions)` over an attached `VisualStateGroups` DP — REUSING the ALREADY-LIVE S510/S512a Storyboard/clock/`BeginStoryboard` engine (S510 delivered `Storyboard`/`DoubleAnimation`/keyframes + `timeline_clock_progress`; S512a delivered `BeginStoryboard` + the live `EventTrigger` Invoke evaluation; 11v later seals the `Timeline`/`Clock` split — a named forward token). A `VisualState`'s per-state visual swap is authored as a `{state, Storyboard}` pair exactly as WPF, so "swap visuals via brushes" becomes a state STORYBOARD animating a brush DP; (2) `GoToState` handles EXIT **correctly** — leaving a state restores the property to its pre-state value, and `useTransitions` true resolves a `VisualTransition` into a dynamic transition Storyboard (the S510 clock reused); (3) state effects are applied through the **animation/trigger band** (NOT a local Set, D4); (4) `ControlTemplate` gains WPF `ValidateTargetType`/`ValidateTemplatedParent` + the default `TargetType = Control` (D5); (5) the `{TemplateBinding}` wiring becomes a real live OneWay binding (the `RelativeSource=TemplatedParent` + property-changed push, coordinated with the 11af binding core) — no discarded read. Each closes the exact drift; the invented `brushProperty`/`enter_state`/`exit_state` engine is REPLACED (the `find_state` convenience keeps a thin forwarding to GoToState for back-compat call sites, recorded), no invented surface is added, and the WPF source is the authority (Rule 1/Rule 2 held).

The app is free to build custom controls for whatever printing/output it needs. ## Sprint 11aq — S401 Button drift closure (content / click-order / owner / enable / state WPF-fidelity)  (goal: the S401 `[DONE]` marker's fidelity claim — "IsEnabled gates Click routing; Click raised on a hit Button; template/visual-state surface (Normal/Hover/Pressed/Disabled swap the Background brush); MeasureOverride bounded default box; classify_merge_element Solid fill" — matches the actual WPF source; the S401 audit residual drift removed)  [token S981+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S401 dep:S400 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Controls\Primitives\ButtonBase.cs` + `...\Controls\Button.cs` + `PresentationCore\System\Windows\UIElement.cs` + `...\Controls\ContentControl.cs`, and the code VAML ships in `Element.cpp` / `InputMarshaller.cpp` / `VamlRenderer.cpp` / `Element.h`):** the S401 `[DONE]` marker overstates fidelity on SEVEN observable axes, each a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must not manufacture Button behavior WPF does not have), not recorded debt:
> - **D1 — Command-vs-Click ORDER (behavioral, the first WPF-fidelity defect the audit caught).** WPF `ButtonBase.OnClick` (`ButtonBase.cs`) raises the bubbling `Click` event FIRST, THEN runs the command: `RaiseEvent(new RoutedEventArgs(ButtonBase.ClickEvent, this)); … ExecuteCommandSource();`. VAML's `Button::raise_click` (`Element.cpp:628-650`) inverts it — it executes `source_command()` then `RaiseEvent(ClickEvent)`. A WPF Click handler observes the command's post-execute side effects; the vaml handler observes pre-execute state. The vaml comment claims "WPF-faithful" while inverting the real source order.
> - **D2 — `IsEnabled` is not command-coerced.** WPF `ButtonBase.IsEnabledCore => base.IsEnabledCore && CanExecute` — a Button whose Command can't execute is effectively disabled. VAML's `is_enabled()` (`Element.cpp:557-559`) is a standalone `int != 0` read independent of the Command, so a WPF button bound to an un-executable command won't click (and its visual shows Disabled) while the vaml one still can.
> - **D3 — DP OWNERSHIP (Rule 3, `(name, ownerType)` — the 11s headline).** WPF registers `Command`/`CommandParameter`/`CommandTarget`/`IsPressed`/`ClickMode` on `ButtonBase` (the 11k-8 audit table) and `IsEnabled` on `UIElement` (11k-8 UIElement surface); `Button.cs` owns only `IsDefault`/`IsCancel`/`IsDefaulted`. VAML's S401 registers `Command`/`CommandParameter`/`CommandTarget`/`IsEnabled` under owner `"Button"`. Under the 11s composite identity those pairs DON'T EXIST in WPF — `DependencyProperty.FromName("Command", typeof(ButtonBase))` never resolves a vaml `Command@Button`. The S401 authors a DP set that WPF would never find.
> - **D4 — NO CONTENT / CONTENTCONTROL model.** WPF `Button : ButtonBase : ContentControl` carries a real `Content`. VAML `class Button final : public UIElement, public ICommandSource` (`Element.h`) has NO `Content` property. 11k-11 authored the GENERIC content-owner routing rule (a single content-owning DP + the `S440 set_content` object slot) and re-bound every single-content container onto it — Button was left out. The `{TemplateBinding}`/`ControlTemplate` closures (11am/11an) therefore have no template-part `Content` on a Button to target.
> - **D5 — MEASURE is content-blind (hardcoded box vs content).** `Button::MeasureOverride` (`Element.cpp`) fabricates `{ 20, 16 }` when `available` is unbound, while the header comment claims it "measures at its natural (content) size" — the code and the comment contradict each other. WPF measures the `ContentPresenter` (`ButtonBase`/`ContentControl` measure path), so a Button sized to its authored content label is impossible today.
> - **D6 — VISUAL-STATE names + disabled look are fabricated.** (a) WPF's state is `MouseOver` (`VisualStates.StateMouseOver`) — VAML uses `"Hover"`, so a consumer/theme keyed to `MouseOver` never matches. (b) WPF adds the `Focused`/`Unfocused` `FocusStates` group; VAML's `ensure_states` builds only the four fill states. (c) the DISABLED fade is a hardcoded `0.55` alpha (`VamlRenderer.cpp:158`) — WPF's disabled look is the theme template's `Disabled` state (a brush, `ThemeResource`), NEVER a library alpha constant, so a themed Disabled brush can't be expressed and every disabled element is forced to 55%. (d) the state preconditions are wrong: WPF selects by real input (`!IsEnabled → IsPressed → IsMouseOver → Normal`, from `VisualStateManager` over the templated control); VAML only swaps on a manual `set_visual_state` call, never auto-transitions on real press/hover.
> - **D7 — the input-trigger model omits capture / `IsPressed` / `ClickMode` / Space-Enter.** WPF raises Click only when `IsPressed && ClickMode == Release` at mouse-up after `CaptureMouse()` + `SetIsPressed(true)` on press, cancels on drag-out (`UpdateIsPressed`), and supports `ClickMode.Press`, Space, Enter. VAML's `InputMarshaller::Push` (MouseUp) raises iff `wasPress && sameElement && !movedAway && withinTolerance && pressed_ != nullptr` — no capture, no `IsPressed` DP, no `ClickMode`, no Space/Enter, drag-cancel approximated by a pixel `moveTolerance_`. The Sprint-8 engine lives in 11ag (below); the S401 raising decision is this sprint's seat.
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint — the contract forces full close, no scoped option):** (1) `OnClick` order corrected — `raise_click` raises the bubbling `Click` FIRST then executes the command (`ButtonBase.OnClick`); (2) `IsEnabled` becomes command-coerced (`IsEnabledCore => base && CanExecute`); (3) the Button DP set is RE-OWNED onto the WPF-true owners (`Command*`/`IsPressed`/`ClickMode` → `ButtonBase`, `IsEnabled` → `UIElement`), coordinating with (not duplicating) the 11n-2 `ICommandSource` real-command-object upgrade; (4) Button gains a content-owning DP routed through 11k-11's GENERIC content-owner rule + a real `Content` object slot via the `S440 set_content` container pattern, so a template part has a Content to target and template bindings/parts resolve as WPF does; (5) `MeasureOverride` measures the CONTENT extent, not a hardcoded box (over a `ContentPresenter`-analogue), with `desired` uncamped per 11ac's S827; (6) the visual-state surface is re-keyed `Hover→MouseOver`, gains the `Focused`/`Unfocused` group, lands its per-state brush swap through the REAL 11am `VisualStateManager.GoToState`/Storyboard model (NOT a bare `Set`, honoring the 11al/11am precedence bands), the invented `0.55` alpha is REMOVED (the Disabled state carries a themed brush / the S400/S-clear alpha path), and the active state is selected from real input preconditions; (7) the Button click decision consumes 11ag's engine (`ClickMode` S872 + capture S874): raise only when `IsPressed && ClickMode==Release` at mouse-up (or `Press`/`Hover` per ClickMode), drag-out cancels via captured pointer, Space/Enter key-click. Each closes the exact drift; no invented surface is added; the WPF source is the authority (Rule 1/Rule 2 held).

> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S402 dep:S401 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Controls\TextBox.cs` + `...\Primitives\TextBoxBase.cs` + `...\Input\KeyboardNavigation.cs` + `...\TextBox.cs`, and the code VAML ships in `Element.cpp` / `Element.h`):** the S402 `[DONE]` marker overstates fidelity on several observable axes, each a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must not manufacture a TextBox WPF does not have), not recorded debt:
> - **D1 — `AcceptsReturn` VALUE-TYPE + `AddOwner` shared-owner drift (the 11s/Rule-3 identity class).** WPF does NOT register `AcceptsReturn` on `TextBlock`-type or as `Text`: it is `KeyboardNavigation.AcceptsReturnProperty.AddOwner(typeof(TextBoxBase))` (`TextBoxBase.cs:466-469`) — a **`bool`-typed** DP whose **effective owner is `TextBoxBase`** (one DP instance SHARED by `TextBox` and `RichTextBox` via the `AddOwner` chain off `KeyboardNavigation`, `KeyboardNavigation.cs:265-276`). SameName/different-owner coexistence (11s) + a shared TextBoxBase owner are both WPF-real and both absent.
> - **D2 — `Text` is `BindsTwoWayByDefault` + `UpdateSourceTrigger.LostFocus`; a plain `{Binding Text}` must be two-way by default.** WPF `TextProperty` (`TextBox.cs:653-668`) registers `FrameworkPropertyMetadataOptions.BindsTwoWayByDefault | Journal` + `UpdateSourceTrigger.LostFocus` — so a `{Binding Text}` (no `Mode=`) is **two-way by default** and the source updates on `LostFocus`. VAML delivers two-way only when the author explicitly writes `Mode=TwoWay` (the S402 test arms `spec.mode = TwoWay`); the `{Binding}` markup default (S252) resolves OneWay, so a plain `{Binding Text}` edit does NOT write back — the exact WPF-observable divergence 11aa S819 (`BindsTwoWayByDefault` runtime effect) was built to close now that the flag has runtime effect.
> - **D3 — caret/selection are CLR/DependencyProperties over a `TextSelection` model, not buried inline fields (the S402 `caret_`/`selStart_`/`selLen_` are invisible member fields).** WPF exposes `CaretIndex` (a settable DP, `TextBox.cs:764-768`), `SelectionStart`/`SelectionLength`, `SelectedText` (a CP over `TextSelection`), `Select(…)/Clear()/ScrollToCaret()` — all first-class, bindable, coerced surface. VAML's caret/selection are un-exposed inline fields that cannot be styled/bound/coerced.
> - **D4 — `TextBoxBase` window: `IsReadOnly`, `IsReadOnlyCaretVisible`, `MaxLength`, `AcceptsTab`, `TextWrapping`, scrollbars, `CharacterCasing`, `TextAlignment`, undo.** The 11k-8 `TextBoxBase`/`TextBox` own-surfaces are audited (IsReadOnly/IsReadOnlyCaretVisible/AcceptsTab/Horizontal+VerticalScrollBarVisibility/IsUndoEnabled/UndoLimit/AutoWordSelection/Selection*/Caret* on TextBoxBase; TextWrapping/MinLines/MaxLines/Text/MaxLength/CharacterCasing/TextAlignment/TextDecorations on TextBox) — registered in the 11k-9 `DpFidelity` table but NOT carried onto a real TextBox control object, so the S402 control's editing semantics cannot honor `MaxLength`, `IsReadOnly`, `TextWrapping`, etc.

## Sprint 11au — S405 ScrollViewer drift closure (bubble/scrollbar / read-only offset+extent DPs / routed ScrollChanged / wheel semantic / content-owner WPF-fidelity)  (goal: the S405 `[DONE]` marker's fidelity claim — "scroll + clipping via clip_to_bounds + wheel/scrollbar + the routed ScrollChanged surface" — matches the actual WPF source; the S405 audit residual drift removed)  [token S1017+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S405 dep:S404 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Controls\ScrollViewer.cs` + `...\Primitives\ScrollBar.cs` + `PresentationCore\System\Windows\UIElement.cs`, and the code VAML ships in `src/core/src/Element.cpp` / `src/core/include/vaml/core/Element.h`):** the S405 `[DONE]` marker overstates fidelity on the exact surface its title names — the "routed ScrollChanged surface," "wheel," "scrollbar," and "clip via clip_to_bounds" — each a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must not manufacture ScrollViewer behavior WPF does not have), not recorded debt:**
- **D1 — the offsets are invented plain `double` members, NOT WPF's read-only dependency properties.** WPF registers `VerticalOffsetProperty`/`HorizontalOffsetProperty` via `DependencyProperty.RegisterReadOnly` + `DependencyPropertyKey` (`ScrollViewer.cs:575-586`) — they can be read via `GetValue`, **coerced**, and **bound**. VAML's `set_vertical_offset`/`vertical_offset()`/`set_horizontal_offset`/`horizontal_offset()` (`Element.cpp`/`Element.h`) are plain `double vertical_`/`horizontal_` member fields with **no `VerticalOffsetProperty`/`HorizontalOffsetProperty` DP**, so `<ScrollViewer VerticalOffset="5">` throws `UnknownProperty` and the offset cannot be bound/coerced.
- **D2 — the `Extent*`/`Viewport*`/`Scrollable*`/`ContentVerticalOffset` read-only DP surface is absent.** WPF exposes `ExtentWidth/HeightProperty`, `ViewportWidth/HeightProperty`, `ScrollableWidth/HeightProperty`, `ContentVerticalOffset/HorizontalOffset` as read-only DPs (`ScrollViewer.cs:609-734`). VAML has only scalar member getters (`content_height()`, `viewport_height()`, `scrollable_height()`) — no DPs, no `ContentVerticalOffset`, no `ScrollableWidth`. Cannot be authored or bound.

> the S406 `[DONE]` marker overstates fidelity on the exact surface its title names — the headline "an unconsumed Enter KEY-DOWN raises the default Button's Click via a FocusManager default-Button" is **not how WPF implements the default button at all**. Each facet below is a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must not manufacture a default-Button mechanism WPF does not have), not recorded debt:
> - **D1 — WPF has NO `FocusManager` `defaultButton_` slot; the default button is WPF's **AccessKey** mechanism on the `Button`.** WPF's default-Button behavior is: `Button.IsDefault` (`Button.cs` — `public static readonly DependencyProperty IsDefaultProperty = DependencyProperty.Register("IsDefault", typeof(bool), typeof(Button), new FrameworkPropertyMetadata(BooleanBoxes.FalseBox, new PropertyChangedCallback(OnIsDefaultChanged)));`) → the change callback `AccessKeyManager.Register("\x000D", button); AccessKeyManager.Unregister("\x000D", button);` (`Button.cs`: register `"\x000D"` = Enter as an AccessKey on the Button). The read-only `IsDefaulted` DP is `IsDefault && KeyboardFocusWithinScope && !KeyboardNavigation.AcceptsReturn`, computed by `UpdateIsDefaulted`/`OnIsDefaultedChanged`. VAML's S406 ships a **per-tree `defaultButton_` member** (`FocusManager.h`) + a `set_default_button(Button*)` the caller inks in — **invented surface with NO WPF counterpart**. `DependencyProperty.FromName("IsDefault", typeof(Button))` never sees a vaml `defaultButton_` slot; there is no `IsDefault` DP and no `"\x000D"` access-key registration.

VAML's `FocusManager::RaiseKeyRouted` raises `KeyDown` on the focused element, then if `!handled` calls `defaultButton_->raise_click()` — a same-call inline path with no `PostProcessInput` stage, so the WPF timing semantics (post-routed-handler, pre-acknowledged) are not reproduced.

Not owned by 11av (11aq S981 owns the order), but 11av must re-verify its default-button Click through the corrected order.
> - **D4 — `IsEnabled` command-coercion absent on the default gate.** WPF activates the default button only when it is enabled AND not command-suppressed (`UpdateIsDefaulted`: `!IsEnabled` → not defaulted + the ButtonBase `IsEnabledCore` command-coercion). VAML's `FocusManager::MoveFocusNext/Previous` walks the visual tree in **pure pre-order** over `UIElement::focusable()` with no `TabIndex`/`IsTabStop` attachment. That is 11ag S873's owned closure (S873 = "FocusManager honors TabIndex + Next/Previous + scope, replacing flat pre-order. Record the tiebreak deviation or align.") — 11av records the S406-over-section as S873's and does NOT re-do it.

## Sprint 11ax — S452 property-element / attribute-element authoring grammar drift closure (split-direction / attached-aware-label / identity-framing WPF-fidelity) + the S453 recorded S7 COMPILED resource-dictionary authoring parity closure (D5)  (goal: the S452 DONE marker's fidelity claim — "<X.Prop> sets the parent DP via the S043 attached-aware path (object→Value::UntypedPtr, literal→convert, empty-skip, unknown-dotted→the structured UnknownProperty error); NOT auto-attached as a visual child" — matches the actual WPF source on the property-element authoring grammar; the S452 audit residual drift removed; AND the S453/S454 recorded "S7 resource-dictionary-authoring parity — resolution at 11b/11x" NO-GAP, never landed in the code path, is finally closed so the S7 compiled VBamlReader authors `<X.Resources>` + `x:Key` + `MergedDictionaries` from the compiled bytes identically to the S2 text reader)  [token S1040+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S452 dep:S451 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against
> `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Markup\XamlReaderHelper.cs` (`SplitPropertyElementName` :1652-1664, the dotted-tag complex-property decision :4482, `CompileComplexProperty`) + `WindowsBase\DependencyProperty.cs` (the `(name, ownerType)` composite identity, `FromNameKey` :251) + the S2/S7 vaml code in `src/core/src/{ParsedElement.cpp,VamlReader.cpp}` + `src/tools/src/{Vamlc.cpp,VBamlReader.cpp}`):**
> the S452 DONE marker overstates fidelity on THREE observable axes the audit caught — the exact "accepted the DONE claim at face value" failure mode the durable WPF-Source-Audit rule exists to forbid. Each is a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must not manufacture a property-element WPF does not have), not recorded debt:
> - **D1 (MATERIAL — the core defect) — the split DIRECTION is INVERTED: `split_property_element` uses `find('.')` (FIRST dot); WPF `SplitPropertyElementName` uses `LastIndexOf('.')` (LAST dot).** VAML's `split_property_element` (`ParsedElement.cpp:322-334`) does `const std::size_t dot = tagName.find('.')` and returns `{substr(0, dot), substr(dot+1)}` — the owner is everything BEFORE the FIRST dot, the property everything AFTER. WPF's `SplitPropertyElementName` (`XamlReaderHelper.cs:1652-1664`) does `int idx = longName.LastIndexOf('.'); ownerName = longName.Substring(0, idx); propName = longName.Substring(idx + 1);` — the owner is everything BEFORE the **LAST** dot, the property the LAST segment. So for `<Foo.Bar.Baz>` WPF resolves owner `"Foo.Bar"` + prop `"Baz"` (`DependencyProperty.FromName("Baz", Foo.Bar)`), while VAML resolves owner `"Foo"` + prop `"Bar.Baz"` — a real WPF document whose authored owner type carries a namespace dot (`clr-namespace` / `assembly:Type.Owner.Prop`, or a `Foo.Bar`-style type) is INVERTED under the first-dot split. The known WPF registered dotted-name DPs don't exist (composite keys are never dotted), so the common `<Button.Background>` one-dot form is unaffected — which is exactly why CI stays green — but any multi-dot authored owner flips owner/property and fires UnknownProperty for a different, wrong key. This is the same class of inversion the 11s/11u/11aa corrective sprints exist to close: the DONE marker's own example works while the grammar beneath it is wrong.
> - **D2 (label) — the DONE marker calls `<X.Prop>` "the S043 attached-aware path"; the actual mechanism does NOT distinguish WPF's OWNED (AddOwner) DP from an ATTACHED DP, so the label overstates fidelity for the very `<Button.Background>` case the title names.** `VamlReader.cpp:1212-1216` resolves the property through `lookup_dp_for_attr(propName, typeName)` — a composite `(name, owner)` read — with NO owned-vs-attached distinction. ## Sprint 11ay — the S453 duplicate-authored-`x:Key` DISPOSITION drift: indexer-OVERWRITE (last-wins) on the resource-dictionary AUTHORING path  (goal: a resource dict re-declaring the same `x:Key` resolves last-wins exactly as WPF's indexer does, on BOTH the S2 text + S7 compiled path — the one S453 authoring gap 11ax deliberately left open)  [token S1050+]

> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS:** the S453/S454 authoring closure (DONE, S2 text path) and the 11ax D5 closure (S1045/S1046, S7 compiled path) captured authored `x:Key` resources via `ResourceDictionary::set(key, value)` — which **THROWS `ResourceAlreadyRegistered` on any duplicate** (`ResourceDictionary.cpp:250-254`: `if (find_self(key) != nullptr) throw ResourceAlreadyRegistered("resource key already registered");`). The S453 DONE note, the 11ax S1045/S1046 tokens, and the parity pins ALL record "duplicate `x:Key` → `ResourceAlreadyRegistered`" as the WPF-faithful disposition. **That is the WPF `Add()` contract, NOT the WPF indexer contract — and the XAML parser writes authored `x:Key` resources through the INDEXER, not `Add()`.** WPF's indexer setter `SetValueWithoutLock` (`ResourceDictionary.cs:429-456`) does `object oldValue = _baseDictionary[key]; if (oldValue != value) { ValidateDeferredResourceReferences(key); ... _baseDictionary[key] = value; }` — it **SILENTLY OVERWRITES** an existing key (last-wins), and `_baseDictionary` is the LibraryDictionary/HybridDictionary that `this[key] = value` routes to. `Add()` (`ResourceDictionary.cs:646` `_baseDictionary.Add(key, value)`, which throws on a duplicate) is NOT the authored-`x:Key` write path. So a real WPF document that re-declares the same `x:Key` within ONE dictionary **loads (last-wins)** in WPF but **throws a hard reader error** in VAML today — a **functional conversion blocker** (a valid WPF doc fails to load) sitting on the authoring path, un-tokenized by S453, by 11ax (which preserved the throw), and by S921 (which targets the PROGRAMMATIC core API `set()`/`set_or_replace()`, i.e. a caller-authored WPF `dict["k"] = v` / `dict.Add`, NOT the parser-authored `x:Key` capture that goes through `build_resource_dictionary`). This sprint closes that exact residual. ## Sprint 11bb — S461 x:Static / x:Type markup-extension drift closure (WPF-faithful tokenization + a real Type object; the C++-registration value fetch recorded as the sanctioned architecture-justified exception)  (goal: the S461 `[DONE]` marker's fidelity claim — "the reader gains register_static_value/ResolveStatic (WPF last-`:`-token lookup) + register_type_value/ResolveType (Value::String type object)" — matches the actual WPF source on the TOKENIZATION + TYPE-IDENTITY axes, with the ONE documented architecture-justified mechanism replacement (VAML is C++, no C# reflection) left as a recorded exception (never silent))  [token S1064+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S461 dep:S460 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-Source-Audit, against
> `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\System.Xaml\System\Windows\Markup\StaticExtension.cs` + `TypeExtension.cs`, and the S461 code in
> `src/core/src/{BindingMarkup.cpp,VamlReader.cpp}` + `test/unit/MarkupStaticType_s461_test.cpp`):** the S461 `[DONE]` marker overstates fidelity on
> TWO observable axes the audit caught, and the THIRD axis is the exact documented-architecture exception this sprint records, NOT closes. Each of the
> two that drifts is a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must not manufacture a tokenization/type-identity scheme WPF does not have), not recorded debt:
> - **D1 (MATERIAL) — the "WPF last-`:`-token lookup" claim is FALSE.** The WPF `{x:Static}` member format is `Prefix:Type.Member`, and the SPLIT is on the DOT, per `StaticExtension.cs`:
> ```csharp
> int dotIndex = _member.IndexOf('.');                     // FIRST dot
> string typeString = _member.Substring(0, dotIndex);       // "local:Constants" — the `:` prefix STAYS in
> ...
> fieldString = _member.Substring(dotIndex + 1, ...);       // "AppName"
> type = xamlTypeResolver.Resolve(typeString);              // the `:` is a NAMESPACE prefix the TYPE resolver consumes
> ```
> The colon is an **XML namespace prefix** consumed by `IXamlTypeResolver` (the S082 clr-namespace model), NOT a token delimiter. VAML's `ResolveStatic` (`VamlReader.cpp:3319-3333`) instead strips the LAST colon (`rfind(':')`, `str.substr(colon+1)` → a flat key `"Constants.AppName"`) and keys a registry on the colon-stripped remainder, with the code comment `// WPF-faithful token resolution` and the DONE parenthetical "WPF last-`:`-token lookup". Both are false — this is exactly the "accepted a label at face value" failure the durable WPF-Source-Audit rule exists to forbid.
> - **D3 (MATERIAL-ish, still a conversion blocker for TYPE IDENTITY) — `{x:Type Button}` returns a String, not a real Type object.** WPF `TypeExtension.cs` resolves and returns a REAL `Type`:
> ```csharp
> _type = xamlTypeResolver.Resolve(_typeName);
> if (_type is null) throw ...   // MarkupExtensionTypeNameBad
> return _type;                  // the Type object
> ```
> VAML's `ResolveType` returns `Value::String(it->second)` built from `register_type_value("Button","Button")` — the "type object" is the class-name STRING (`MarkupStaticType_s461_test.cpp` registers the String). The S461 title's "type object for TargetType / ContentControl binding" + the implicit-style Type-key (11al S943) + type-keyed resources therefore rest on a String, with no real Type identity.
> - **D2 — the EXCLUDED AXIS (the DOCUMENTED, ARCHITECTURE-JUSTIFIED MECHANISM REPLACEMENT, NOT closed here).** WPF `{x:Static}` FETCHES the static field/const/value by REFLECTION — `type.IsEnum → Enum.Parse` + `GetFieldOrPropertyValue` walking `currentType.BaseType`, plus the `MemberType` direct-type form (`StaticExtension.cs:92-131, :157-176`). VAML is a C++ translation with NO C# reflection, so a `{x:Static}` VALUE is app/reader-REGISTERED (`register_static_value`) rather than reflected. This is the mechanism replacement explicitly EXEMPTED: architecture-justified per the S250 "engineer wires, we bind" pattern (Rule 1 applies to the observable contract; the C++ registration value-path is the sanctioned adaptation). This sprint makes the TOKENIZATION of the static member (D1) + the TYPE identity of `{x:Type}` (D3) WPF-faithful, and it RECORDS D2 as the WPF-reflected-but-C++-registered surface — the enum-parse special-case, the base-type static walk, and the `MemberType` direct-type form are documented as the non-mirrored reflection surface, never silent.
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint — the contract forces full close of D1 + D3; D2 stays the recorded exception):** (1) the static-member tokenization is re-written to the WPF first-dot grammar — split `{x:Static Prefix:Type.Member}` on the FIRST `.`, carry the `Prefix:` as a NAMESPACE prefix resolved through the S082 clr-namespace / namespace→type table (the type resolver), member = after the first dot; (2) a static member VALUE resolves against its OWNED (namespace-resolved) TYPE under the 11s composite `(name, owner)` + the 11al Type-token store — the flat colon-stripped single-key registry is retired; (3) `{x:Type}` returns a REAL Type identity (a `Value::Type` payload resolved through the composite/Type-token reader), replaced from `Value::String`, so TargetType/ContentControl/implicit-style/type-keyed-resource identity keys on a real Type; (4) D2 recorded as the sanctioned exception. Each closes the exact (non-exempt) drift; no invented surface is added; the WPF source is the authority (Rule 1/Rule 2 held).
> **RELATION TO 11s/11t/11al/11af/11ai/11z:** 11s owns composite `(name, ownerType)` identity (S800-S808 — the owned-type key the static member + the Type identity resolve through); 11t owns the value-pipeline order + the strict-synchronous `with_changed` model; **11al S943 owns the Type-token implicit-style surface** (`FrameworkElement.cs:1867` — `{x:Type}`'s Type identity must key the SAME token store so `TargetType`/implicit-style/type-keyed resources agree); 11af owns the `PropertyPath` grammar (S845+, disjoint — the static member is a member path into a type, recorded not-opened); 11ai owns the `vaml::` exception base (the Class A unresolved/malformed static/type errors). 11bb is independent of 11s/11t/11u (no identity-key change, no pipeline-order change, no thread change) — it closes the S461-MARKUP-EXTENSION-SPECIFIC residual (D1/D3) ON TOP of those closures, exactly as the S-series siblings closed their S### residuals. **D2 is the recorded architecture-justified exception, NOT re-litigated — the value fetch stays C++-registered (S1068 is a record-only step).** ZERO new locks (ADR-018 — single-threaded registration + Set-time + resolve, the S126 affinity model unchanged). ## Sprint 11bd — S463 EVENT-ATTRIBUTE drift closure (Window.Closing as a non-routed CLR event / Loaded as Direct+per-node / TextChanged-raise-on-programmatic-set / the RAISED-ATTACHED authoring WPF-fidelity)  (goal: the S463 `[DONE]` marker's fidelity claim — "RoutedEvent gains the authored-set bubbling identities LoadedEvent/ClosingEvent/TextChangedEvent; the S322 BindEvents table extends to Loaded/Closing/TextChanged; the RAISED-ATTACHED form StackPanel.Button.Click (WPF-faithful bubbling attach over the Sprint-8 engine)" — matches the actual WPF source for each authored EVENT-ATTRIBUTE identity and for the raised-attached authoring grammar; the S463 audit residual drift removed)  [token S1080+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S463 dep:S462 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-Source-Audit, against `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Window.cs` + `PresentationFramework\System\Windows\FrameworkElement.cs` + `PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Controls\Primitives\TextBoxBase.cs` + `System.Windows.Input\Extension\Mouse.cs` + `PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Markup\XamlReaderHelper.cs`, and the code VAML ships in `src/core/src/RoutedEvent.cpp` + `Element.cpp` (the authored-set event identities, `raise_loaded`/`raise_closing`/`raise_text_changed`, the S322 BindEvents table) + the event-tail routing in the VAML reader):** the S463 `[DONE]` marker overstates fidelity on FOUR observable axes the audit caught — the exact "accepted a WPF-faithful label at face value" failure the durable WPF-Source-Audit rule exists to forbid, and each is a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must not manufacture an event identity WPF does not have, and must not represent an event WPF models very differently as a bubbling RoutedEvent), not recorded debt:
> - **D1 (MATERIAL) — `Window.Closing` is NOT a Routed Event at all; it is a plain CLR event with `CancelEventHandler`.** WPF `Window.cs`: `public event CancelEventHandler Closing { add { Events.AddHandler(EVENT_CLOSING, value); } remove { Events.RemoveHandler(EVENT_CLOSING, value); } }` — a **plain CLR event** (signature `CancelEventHandler(object, CancelEventArgs)`), with **no `RoutedEvent`**, no route strategy, no `RaiseEvent`, and **no `handled` stop-flag**. It is raised via `OnClosing(CancelEventArgs e)` → `handler(this, e)` (Window.cs:2038-2041), and the args are `CancelEventArgs` with a `.Cancel` property (setting `e.Cancel = true` dismisses the window, Window.cs:2205). VAML's S463 registered `ClosingEvent` as a **Bubbling routed event** (`RoutedEvent.cpp:101-104`) raised through `RaiseEvent` with a `handled` return that the test even asserts. Two observables diverge: (a) the handler signature is `CancellableEventArgs`, not `RoutedEventArgs`; (b) there is NO route to bubble and NO `handled`-stops-anything — cancel is the dismiss, never a stop-flag. The `([DONE] ... Closing)` claim modeled a non-routed CLR event as a bubbling RoutedEvent — the direct analogue of the D-the-audit-checks writes, here on the Window.
> - **D2 (MATERIAL) — `Loaded` is `RoutingStrategy.Direct` + per-node tree broadcast, NOT Bubble.** WPF `FrameworkElement.cs:5699`: `public static readonly RoutedEvent LoadedEvent = EventManager.RegisterRoutedEvent("Loaded", RoutingStrategy.Direct, typeof(RoutedEventHandler), _typeofThis);` — `Loaded` is **`RoutingStrategy.Direct`**, it does NOT travel the parent chain, and VAML's `raise_loaded()` bubbling the event UP to the Window's ancestors (`RoutedEvent.cpp:96` + the ancestor-climb in `Element.cpp`) inverts WPF. WPF raises `Loaded` by a **tree broadcast** — `BroadcastEventHelper.BroadcastEvent` (BroadcastEventHelper.cs:251-280) collects the whole loaded subtree and calls `fo.OnLoaded(args)` on EACH node individually (Direct, `new RoutedEventArgs(routedEvent, d)` per node with source == that node, BroadcastEventHelper.cs:262). So `Loaded` on a Window fires per-node across the loaded tree, never bubbles to an ancestor.
> - **D3 (MATERIAL) — `TextChanged` is Bubble (CORRECT), but the raise TRIGGER is wrong: WPF raises it on ANY text-content mutation, including a programmatic `Text` set; VAML raises it only from a key edit commit.** WPF `TextBoxBase.cs:901-906`: `public static readonly RoutedEvent TextChangedEvent = EventManager.RegisterRoutedEvent("TextChanged", RoutingStrategy.Bubble, typeof(TextChangedEventHandler), typeof(TextBoxBase));` — Bubble (VAML's strategy matches). BUT WPF raises it from `OnTextChanged` called by `TextContainer.Changed` (TextBoxBase.cs:1395), which fires whenever the text content mutates, REGARDLESS of input source. VAML's `raise_text_changed()` fires only inside `handle_key` on a REAL edit commit (`Element.cpp:1637`), so `tb.set_text("x")` sets the Text DP and does NOT raise `TextChanged` — the exact ubiquitous WPF observable (a `Text="..."` assignment raises TextChanged) is missing for TextBox. (The S402 `Text` DP is `BindsTwoWayByDefault` per 11ar S991, but that is the write-back trigger, NOT the raise trigger.)
> - **D4 (MATERIAL) — the RAISED-ATTACHED `StackPanel.Button.Click` triple-dot form is NOT WPF syntax; WPF splits an attribute owner on the LAST dot and resolves the owner as a TYPE.** WPF `XamlReaderHelper.cs` `SplitPropertyElementName` (:1652-1664): `int idx = longName.LastIndexOf('.'); ownerName = longName.Substring(0, idx); propName = longName.Substring(idx + 1);` — so `StackPanel.Button.Click` resolves owner = `"StackPanel.Button"` + prop = `"Click"`, and `GetClrInfoForClass` tries to resolve a TYPE literally named `StackPanel.Button` (no such type) → WPF throws. The valid WPF attached-event form is TWO segments: `Owner.Event` where `Owner` is a type exposing a static `Add<Event>Handler(DependencyObject, handler)` (e.g. `Mouse.cs:151` `public static void AddMouseDownHandler(DependencyObject element, MouseButtonEventHandler handler)` → `Mouse.MouseDown="handler"`); and `Button.Click="handler"` is valid as an INSTANCE event (ButtonBase.cs:175 ClickEvent) ON the Button, never an attach on an ancestor. VAML's S463 invented a `Type.Owner.Event` triple-dot grammar (event-tail routing on the last dotted segment) that WPF does not have, filed "WPF-faithful bubbling attach" — the label is not supported by the source for that exact grammar. The INTENT (an ancestor capturing a child Button's bubbled Click) is real WPF (registering a bubbling handler on the ancestor / `AddHandler(Button.ClickEvent, ..., handledEventsToo)`), but the AUTHORING-GRAMMAR is a VAML original, not WPF markup.
> **HOLDS (D5 — the part of S463 that does NOT drift, recorded NOT re-opened):** `TextChanged` is genuinely Bubbling (D3's strategy half — VAML's S402/S463 Bubble registration matches `TextBoxBase.cs:901-906`); the S322 `BindEvents`/`register_event`/`bind_class_handler` markup-event wiring mechanism (a handler name resolved on the x:Class owner, a keyed event attribute routed, deferred-event resolution) is real and WPF-consistent for INSTANCE events; the `Button.Click` instance-event form authored ON a Button raises + bubbles correctly (S401/S324 flow); a child Button's raised `Click` bubbles to its ancestors through the routed engine. These are pinned by the parity test in this sprint.
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint — the contract forces full close, no scoped option):** (1) `Window.Closing` is re-modeled as a **non-routed, cancelable CLR event** (a `window_closing`-style `CancelEventHandler`-analogue carrying a `Cancel` bool; args authored with `CancelEventArgs`-faithful `.Cancel`; set-Cancel dismisses) — `ClosingEvent` is REMOVED from the bubbling `RoutedEvent` table, the `handled` stop-flag is retired for it, and the S322 markup event `Closing="..."` wires a CLR-Delegate subscription, not a routed handler (D1); ## Sprint 11bh — S470 DockPanel drift closure (live `LastChildFill` / WPF-faithful remaining-bounds Measure offer / DONE-marker honesty WPF-fidelity)  (goal: the S470 `[DONE]` marker's fidelity claim — "`Dock` attached DP (Left/Right/Top/Bottom/Fill) + Measure/Arrange stacking children by dock order; classify_element → Solid" — matches the actual WPF source; the S470 audit residual drift removed)  [token S1106+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S470 dep:S466 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Controls\DockPanel.cs`, and the code VAML ships in `src/core/src/Element.cpp` / `src/core/include/vaml/core/Element.h` / `src/core/src/ElementDpFidelity.cpp`):** the S470 `[DONE]` marker overstates fidelity on THREE observable axes, and its own title names one — "LastChildFill" is conspicuously absent from the delivered surface even though the marker claims "resolves the S462 DockPanel.Dock NO-GAP". Each axis below is a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must not manufacture a DockPanel WPF does not have), not recorded debt:
> - **D1 (MATERIAL — the headline) — `LastChildFill` is REGISTERED but never READ: the ArrangeOverride hard-codes last-child-fill.** WPF's `DockPanel.cs` `ArrangeOverride` gates the fill on the real bool DP: `int nonFillChildrenCount = totalChildrenCount - (LastChildFill ? 1 : 0); if (i < nonFillChildrenCount) { switch (GetDock(child)) { ... } } else { /* fill child — the remaining interior */ }` — `LastChildFill` is a live `DependencyProperty.Register("LastChildFill", typeof(bool), typeof(DockPanel), ... default true)` (`DockPanel.cs` `LastChildFillProperty`). VAML's `ElementDpFidelity.cpp` registers `LastChildFill` (as `ValueType::Int32` default `1`, the "Bool via Int32" convention) but **no code path ever reads it** — `Element.cpp`'s `ArrangeOverride` uses a hard-coded `const bool isLast = (i + 1 == n)` fill test and there is no `last_child_fill()`/`set_last_child_fill()` accessor. So an authored `DockPanel LastChildFill="False"` (the WPF corpus bool form) resolves the DP but the panel STILL fills its last child — WPF would dock that last child to its `Dock` edge instead. This is the exact "registered-but-unconsumed" class of error the roadmap rails against elsewhere, and the `[11r EXHAUSTIVE: S649 DockPanel ×2 xaml instances]` gate stays green only because both placement classes exercise the default (true) fill.
> - **D2 (material-ish) — Measure offers children UNBOUNDED (`Size::Infinite()` on both axes); WPF offers the REMAINING (bounded) constraint.** WPF `DockPanel.cs` `MeasureOverride` builds the per-child offer as `childConstraint = new Size(Math.Max(0.0, constraint.Width - accumulatedWidth), Math.Max(0.0, constraint.Height - accumulatedHeight)); child.Measure(childConstraint);` then accumulates the docked child's `DesiredSize` into the track. VAML's `Element.cpp` `MeasureOverride` offers `Size::Infinite()` on BOTH axes (the header rationalizes it as "the S123 infinity rule") — so a child whose natural extent exceeds the panel's remaining offer is measured at its FULL natural size and never reports the panel's remaining bound, over-inflating `parentWidth`/`parentHeight` vs. WPF. (This is distinct from, and COMPOSES WITH, the 11ac S827 "DesiredSize may exceed available, not clamped" correction: S827 governs the Return value; D2 governs the OFFER handed into `Measure`. A wrap-to-available TextBlock offered `∞` wraps to content; offered the remaining bounds it wraps to the dock panel's leftover track — observably different.)
> - **D3 (claim/comment) — the header's "WPF-FAITHFUL ALGORITHM" label and the `Dock` enum comment overstate what shipped.** `Element.h` bills the unbounded-MEASURE + hard-coded-fill ARRANGE as "WPF-FAITHFUL ALGORITHM" while both diverge (D1/D2); and the `Dock` enum comment correctly notes "there is NO `Fill` member" (WPF `public enum Dock { Left, Top, Right, Bottom }` — correct) but frames fill as keyed position (`isLast`) which is only WPF-true when `LastChildFill == true` — a mechanism the code never consults. The `Dock` ATTACHED DP itself is WPF-faithful and HOLDS (D4 below).
> **HOLDS (D4 — the part of S470 that does NOT drift, recorded NOT re-opened + pinned):** the `Dock` attached DP matches the WPF source — `public enum Dock { Left, Top, Right, Bottom }` (NO `Fill` member — correct, `Fill` is positional via `LastChildFill`, not a `Dock` value); `DockProperty = DependencyProperty.RegisterAttached("Dock", typeof(Dock), typeof(DockPanel), new FrameworkPropertyMetadata(Dock.Left, ...), new ValidateValueCallback(IsValidDock))` — owner `"DockPanel"`, default `Dock.Left`, range validator accepting exactly Left/Top/Right/Bottom (VAML's `with_validate(x>=0&&x<=3)` is the equivalent domain; the 11t S810_1 disposition makes an out-of-range authoring THROW `InvalidPropertyValueException`, matching WPF's `ArgumentException(InvalidPropertyValue)`); and the attach resolves on any object (S043, the `RegisterAttached` semantics). `classify_element → Solid` + the S470 DONE-marker's `(name, owner)` identity hold. These are pinned by an explicit parity test in S1108, never re-audited as drift.
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint — the contract forces full close, no scoped option):** (1) `LastChildFill` becomes a LIVE, READ surface: the `ArrangeOverride` gates the fill on the boolean `LastChildFill` exactly as `DockPanel.cs` (`nonFillChildrenCount = totalChildrenCount - (LastChildFill ? 1 : 0)`), the hard-coded `isLast` fill test is REMOVED, the DP is retyped to WPF's `bool` (the 11ar S990 "Bool not Int32" precedent), and a typed `set_last_child_fill`/`last_child_fill()` accessor lands — so `LastChildFill="False"` docks the last child to ITS dock edge; (2) the `MeasureOverride` offer is corrected to the WPF remaining-bounds `childConstraint` (`max(0, constraint − accumulated)` per axis), composing with the 11ac S827/S828 measure corrections, so a docked child measures against the panel's leftover track; (3) the "WPF-FAITHFUL ALGORITHM"/position-is-fill comment claims are corrected to the real mechanism (last-child-fill is a `LastChildFill`-gated DECISION, not a position invariant), history preserved un-edited per the S167_1 corrective convention. Each closes the exact drift; no invented surface is added; the WPF source (`DockPanel.cs`) is the authority (Rule 1/Rule 2 held; Rule 3 held — the `Dock`/`LastChildFill` DPs key `(name, ownerType=DockPanel)` per the 11s composite store).
> **RELATION TO 11s/11t/11u/11aa/11ab/11ac/11ad/11ae/11ag/11ai/11k-11/11r/11z:** 11s owns composite `(name, ownerType)` identity (S800-S808 — the `(Dock, DockPanel)`/`(LastChildFill, DockPanel)` pair-keyed store + `resolve_target_id`); 11t owns the value-pipeline order + the strict-synchronous `with_changed` model + the S810_1 validation-throw disposition; 11ac owns the DesiredSize-not-clamped + Stretch-to-arrange measure corrections (S827/S828 — D2 RE-BASES onto these, it does not re-litigate them); 11ad owns the conditional-clip/`ClipToBounds` + `needs_clip` arrange model (S832-S835 — the DockPanel fill child's child-wins-then-clip squeeze rides it); 11ae owns the `ArrangeOverride`-returns-`Size` + RenderSize/ink + `FrameworkElement`-seam node (S841/S842 — the DockPanel override re-bases onto the post-11ae FE seam); 11ag owns the Sprint-8 routed-event/input engine; 11ai owns the `vaml::` exception base (the S810_1 `InvalidPropertyValueException` the Dock validator throws); 11k-11 owns the generic content-owner routing (DockPanel is a `Panel`, not a content-owner — its children are the docked items via the S121 visual children list, NO S440 `set_content` slot, recorded); 11r S649 owns the `[11r EXHAUSTIVE: S649 DockPanel ×2 xaml instances]` scan queue (S1108's `LastChildFill="False"` instance is added to re-cover the placement class the ×2 gate never scanned). 11bh is independent of 11s/11t/11u/11aa/11ab (no identity-key change, no pipeline-order change, no thread change, no base-ownership move) — it closes the S470-DockPanel-SPECIFIC residual (D1/D2/D3) ON TOP of those closures, exactly as 11aq/11ar/11as/11at/11au/11av closed their S### residuals. 11z's executor seam untouched. ZERO new locks (ADR-018 — single-threaded registration + Set-time + measure/arrange, the S126 affinity model unchanged). The AUDIT SPLIT (recorded per the revised-audit discipline): the **ToggleButton-inherited** surface — `IsChecked` as WPF `bool?` (null = third state), `IsThreeState`/`Indeterminate`, the real `Checked`/`Unchecked`/`Indeterminate` bubbling RoutedEvents (11at S1011's `"\1"` fix), `BindsTwoWayByDefault` on `IsChecked` (11aa S819), the content-owner `Content` label (11k-11 / 11at S1012), and the `SetCurrentValue` toggle band — is OWNED BY **Sprint 11at S1010–S1013 / 11k-11 / 11aa** and is a recorded hand-off, NOT re-litigated here. 11bi owns ONLY what no other step owns:
> - **D1 (MATERIAL — the headline) — `GroupName` (the actual WPF group mechanism) is entirely ABSENT.** WPF's exclusivity is keyed on the explicit string `GroupName` (`RadioButton.cs` `GroupNameProperty = DependencyProperty.Register("GroupName", typeof(string), typeof(RadioButton), new FrameworkPropertyMetadata(String.Empty, new PropertyChangedCallback(OnGroupNameChanged)))`), with `OnGroupNameChanged`/`Register`/`Unregister` moving the button into a **global thread-static `_groupNameToElements` weak-reference `Hashtable`** keyed by groupName, and `UpdateRadioButtonGroup()` unchecks name-grouped peers that share `KeyboardNavigation.GetVisualRoot(rb)`. VAML ships ONLY the empty-group single-parent model — there is **no `GroupName` DP, no `_groupNameToElements` registry, no named-group scoping anywhere** (`src/core` grep: zero `GroupName` hits), and the `Element.h` header comment defers it openly as NO-GAP. So a real WPF `.xaml` that authors `<RadioButton GroupName="ChoiceGroup"/>` cannot express the group at all — the S471 flat `✅ DONE` marker names "group semantics" while WPF's headline group mechanism does not exist.
> - **D2 (material) — empty-group scope is VISUAL-parent direct siblings; WPF is LOGICAL-parent children.** VAML `set_checked` (`Element.cpp:2988-3011`) clears `dynamic_cast<RadioButton*>` SIBLINGS under `parent()` (the immediate VISUAL parent). WPF's `UpdateRadioButtonGroup` empty-group arm walks `RadioButton` children of the **LOGICAL parent**: `parent = this.Parent; children = LogicalTreeHelper.GetChildren(parent);` — unchecking empty-group RadioButton children of the logical Parent. The two coincide only when the visual and logical trees are the same flat layer; under a logical parent that is not the immediate visual parent (or with non-RadioButton logical children between), VAML diverges observably from WPF.
> - **D3 (event-fidelity defect) — exclusive-clearing a sibling does NOT raise `Unchecked` on that sibling.** WPF's `UncheckRadioButton()` → `SetCurrentValueInternal(IsCheckedProperty, false)` flows through `ToggleButton.OnIsCheckedChanged` (the DP property-changed callback), so the previously-checked SIBLING raises its own `Unchecked` RoutedEvent with `source == that sibling`. VAML's `set_checked(true)` clears each checked sibling via a BARE `rb->Set(PropertyId::of("IsChecked","RadioButton"), Value::Int32(0))` (`:3006`) and calls `apply_change(value)` ONLY on `this` (`:3012`) — the cleared sibling emits **no routed event at all**. And `RadioButton_test.cpp` / the `[11r EXHAUSTIVE: S661 RadioButton ×3 xaml instances]` gate assert `is_checked()` values only — they never subscribe to `Unchecked` on the cleared sibling — so this gap is green-on-CI. In WPF a handler on the cleared sibling's `Unchecked=` fires; in VAML it never does.
> - **D4 (click semantics) — the never-uncheck-by-click (`OnToggle`) contract is absent.** WPF `RadioButton.OnToggle()` always does `SetCurrentValueInternal(IsCheckedProperty, TrueBox)` — a second click on the ALREADY-CHECKED button does **NOT** uncheck it (unlike CheckBox, whose 11at toggle cycles). VAML's RadioButton has no `OnToggle`/click-wire in the S471 surface at all, and the 11at CheckBox toggle closure does NOT carry over (that is CheckBox's own click cycle). So the WPF-observable "a RadioButton in a group cannot be clicked off" contract is neither implemented nor recorded.
> **HOLDS (D5 — the part of S471 that does NOT drift, recorded NOT re-opened + pinned):** the `IsChecked` DP registration resolves under OWNER `"RadioButton"` (`register_radiobutton_properties` at `Element.cpp:400`, `PropertyId::of("IsChecked","RadioButton")`) — consistent with the 11s/11at Rule-3 composite `(name, owner)` identity; the routed `Checked`/`Unchecked` identities are registered `RouteEventDirection::Bubble` with `source == this` on the checked button (`Element.cpp:403-404`, `apply_change` `:2973`), matching the WPF `CheckedEvent`/`UncheckedEvent` `RoutingStrategy.Bubble` on the state-changing button; the failed `GroupName`-absent axis `D1` + the parent-sibling `D2` + the silent-sibling `D3` + the never-uncheck `D4` are the RESIDUAL, with only the ToggleButton-inherited axes re-pointed to 11at. These are pinned by an explicit parity test in S1112, never re-audited as drift.
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint — the contract forces full close, no scoped option):** (1) introduce the real `GroupName` string DP (owner `RadioButton`, default `""`, `WithDefault(String)`) with WPF-faithful `OnGroupNameChanged` semantics — a global name→group registry of weak references (`_groupNameToElements`-analogue) into which a button `Register`/`Unregister`s on group-name change, and make exclusivity scope by `GroupName`: a NON-empty group resolves peers via the name registry sharing the visual root; the empty `""` group falls to WPF's LOGICAL-parent children walk (D2); (2) re-key the empty-group exclusivity off the visual-parent-siblings walk onto the LOGICAL-parent children arm — `parents chain` → `LogicalTreeHelper.GetChildren`-analogue walking the logical parent's RadioButton children so the scope matches WPF under a nested logical tree; (3) add the sibling `Unchecked` raise — when `set_checked(true)` clears a checked RadioButton sibling, that sibling raises its OWN `Unchecked` RoutedEvent (`source == that sibling`), exactly WPF's DP-callback path — so a handler authored on the cleared sibling's `Unchecked=` actually fires, and extend the `[11r EXHAUSTIVE: S661 RadioButton ×3 xaml instances]` gate to assert the sibling `Unchecked` fires (never green-on-CI for that axis); (4) add the `OnToggle` never-uncheck click path — a click on the checked button keeps it checked (WPF `RadioButton.OnToggle` = always-true), distinct from CheckBox's toggle (11at is NOT re-litigated; the 11ag/11aq click engine consumed, not re-authored). Each closes the exact drift; no invented surface is added; the WPF source (`RadioButton.cs` + `ToggleButton.cs`) is the authority (Rule 1/Rule 2 held; Rule 3 held — the `GroupName`/`IsChecked` DPs key `(name, ownerType=RadioButton)` per the 11s composite store).

## Sprint 11bj — S472 ComboBox drift closure (Selector/ItemsControl items model / object SelectedItem / SelectionChangedEventArgs payload / IsDropDownOpen dropdown surface WPF-fidelity)  (goal: the S472 `[DONE]` marker's fidelity claim — "ItemsSource/Items + SelectionChanged + dropdown interaction" — matches the actual WPF source; the S472 audit residual drift removed)  [token S1114+]

> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S472 dep:S471 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Controls\ComboBox.cs` + `...\Controls\Primitives\Selector.cs` + `...\Controls\ItemsControl.cs`, and the code VAML ships in `src/core/src/Element.cpp` (ComboBox ctor + `split_items` at :3030-3180, `register_combo_properties`) / `src/core/include/vaml/core/Element.h`):** the S472 `[DONE]` marker overstates fidelity on the exact surfaces its title names, each a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must be able to express a real WPF ComboBox document, not a comma-split string model), not recorded debt. The AUDIT SPLIT (recorded per the revised-audit discipline): the **content/editable chrome** sub-axis of ComboBox (the editable TextBox part + the `SelectionBoxItem`/`SelectionBoxItemTemplate` read-only DP surface) is recorded NO-GAP to the S649-list / 11k-11 generic content-owner routing continuation, NOT re-litigated here. 11bj owns ONLY what no other step owns — the items/selection/dropdown model:
>
> - **D1 — `ItemsControl`/`Selector` base + the `Items`/`ItemsSource` ITEMS MODEL is a comma-split String, not WPF's collection.** WPF `public class ComboBox : Selector` (ComboBox.cs:29), `public abstract class Selector : ItemsControl` (Selector.cs:26), `public class ItemsControl : Control` (ItemsControl.cs:34); `ItemsSourceProperty = DependencyProperty.Register("ItemsSource", typeof(IEnumerable), typeof(ItemsControl), ...)` (ItemsControl.cs:176) and the live `Items` is an **`ItemCollection`** (ItemsControl.cs:107), never a settable string DP. VAML registers `(Items, ComboBox)` and `(ItemsSource, ComboBox)` as **String** DPs split on commas/whitespace (`split_items`, Element.cpp:3039-3061) and ComboBox has NO `ItemsControl`/`Selector` base. A corpus `<ComboBox ItemsSource="{Binding MyList}">` or with multiple `<ComboBoxItem>` children cannot be represented. The S472-recorded deferral — "the WPF ItemCollection model is consumed at S649" — points at a **phantom token**: S649 was re-bound + resolved at 11k-11 as generic content routing, which does NOT schedule ComboBox's collection/selection model (the recorded NO-GAP is effectively not a real resolution point). The collection machinery that already exists in the repo (`ItemsControl.h`/`ItemsControl.cpp`, `ObservableCollection`/`CollectionView` from 11n-4, `ContentPresenter`+DataContext-inheritance from S500) is **not wired onto ComboBox**. (ListBox/ListView share the same `Selector` items/selection model — S473's residual is LISTED in the 11bj RELATION as a forward hand-off, closed here on the shared Selector base they both inherit.)
> - **D2 — `SelectedIndex`/`SelectedItem` are NOT owned DPs; `SelectedItem` is a String, not WPF's `object`.** WPF `SelectedIndexProperty` (Selector.cs:306, `typeof(int)`) + `SelectedItemProperty` (Selector.cs:362, `typeof(object)`) live on `Selector`; VAML ships a String `(SelectedItem, ComboBox)` synced from the flattened split list and no `(SelectedIndex, ComboBox)` int DP. A corpus `SelectedItem="{Binding x}"` binds an **object**; VAML stores only a String. Under the composite `(name, ownerType)` rule (Rule 3), `DependencyProperty.FromName("SelectedItem", typeof(Selector))` would never resolve VAML's `(SelectedItem, ComboBox)` — the 11s re-key touched the engine, not re-homed these DPs onto the `Selector` owner.
> - **D3 — `SelectionChanged` carries a BARE `RoutedEventArgs`; WPF's carries `SelectionChangedEventArgs` with the Added/Removed items.** WPF `SelectionChangedEvent = EventManager.RegisterRoutedEvent("SelectionChanged", RoutingStrategy.Bubble, typeof(SelectionChangedEventHandler), typeof(Selector))` (Selector.cs:75-76) with a `SelectionChangedEventArgs` exposing `AddedItems`/`RemovedItems` (the delta, source==the Selector). VAML raises bare `RoutedEventArgs` (`apply_selection`, :3096-3105) — a handled-route with no added/removed payload, so a `SelectionChanged` handler cannot observe the WPF delta.
> - **D4 — the DROPDOWN surface uses the INVENTED `(IsOpen, ComboBox)` Int32; WPF uses the coerced bool `IsDropDownOpen` + `MaxDropDownHeight`.** WPF ComboBox own DPs: `IsDropDownOpen` (ComboBox.cs:105 — a `bool` coerced via `CoerceIsDropDownOpen` at :149-163) + `MaxDropDownHeight` (ComboBox.cs:81, `double`) + the CLR (non-routed) `DropDownOpened`/`DropDownClosed` (ComboBox.cs:503-513). VAML invented `(IsOpen, ComboBox)` Int32 `[0,1]` — a name WPF never registers (WPF has NO `IsOpen`). The 11k-9 `DpFidelity` table registered `IsDropDownOpen`/`MaxDropDownHeight` as RESOLVABLE names (so an authored `IsDropDownOpen="True"` no longer throws UnknownProperty) but wired NO behavior — the dropdown corpus drives a dead DP.
>
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint — the contract forces full close, no scoped option):** (1) introduce the WPF `Selector : ItemsControl` base chain and register `ItemsSource`/`Items` (owner `ItemsControl`, `IEnumerable`/`ItemCollection` object model, NOT String) + `SelectedIndex`/`SelectedItem` (owner `Selector`; `SelectedItem` = `object`, not String), re-homing the ComboBox DPs onto their WPF owners per the 11s `(name, ownerType)` contract; (2) wire the collection machinery the repo already ships (the S500/11n-4 `ObservableCollection`/`CollectionView` + `ItemsControl` + `ContentPresenter`) so an authored `ItemsSource="{Binding MyList}"`, multiple `<ComboBoxItem>` children, and a bound `SelectedItem` express the real WPF item/selection model; (3) raise `SelectionChanged` with a `SelectionChangedEventArgs`-analogue carrying `AddedItems`/`RemovedItems` (the delta, source==the Selector), and make the S472 test subscribe the routed event (no green-on-CI hole); (4) add the WPF-true `IsDropDownOpen` (bool, coerced via the `CoerceIsDropDownOpen`-analogue) + `MaxDropDownHeight` DPs, replacing the invented `(IsOpen, ComboBox)` — so an authored `IsDropDownOpen="True"` actually drives `open()`/`is_open()`. The `SelectionBox*`/editable-chrome surface is recorded NO-GAP to the S649-list / 11k-11 content-owner continuation, never silent. Each closes the exact drift; no invented surface is added; the WPF source (`ComboBox.cs` + `Selector.cs` + `ItemsControl.cs`) is the authority (Rule 1/Rule 2 held; Rule 3 held — the DPs key `(name, ownerType=ItemsControl/Selector/ComboBox)` per the 11s composite store).
