## Sprint 11bl — S481 Border drift closure (Background AddOwner + interior fill / non-uniform BorderThickness / CornerRadius type + non-uniform corners / null-and-zero-thickness render-nothing / Affects* metadata WPF-fidelity)  (goal: the S481 `System.Windows.Controls.Border` `[DONE]` marker's fidelity claim matches the actual WPF `Border.cs` on EVERY axis the marker names and the S481 sprint pipeline delivered; the S481 audit residual drift removed end-to-end)  [token S1124+]

> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S481 dep:S480 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Controls\Border.cs` and the code VAML ships in `src/core/src/Element.cpp` (`register_border_properties`, `Border::MeasureOverride`/`ArrangeOverride`) / `src/core/include/vaml/core/Element.h` (`Border`) / `src/presentation/src/VamlRenderer.cpp` (classifier emits `border_rect`) / `src/vulkan/src/ui/UiPipeline.cpp` (the S205 `border_style`/`border_coverage` authority)):** the S481 `[DONE]` marker overstates fidelity on FOUR observable axes, each a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML cannot express WPF's signature `<Border Background="...">` filled border, nor a non-uniform / null-brush / rounded-corner border the way WPF draws it), not recorded debt. The AUDIT SPLIT (recorded per the revised-audit discipline, Rule 3 held — the composite `(name, ownerType)` identity is correctly applied at S481, NOT re-litigated here): the **composite DP identity** (`Border.Padding` coexists with `Control.Padding`), the **single-child content slot**, and the **measure/arrange combined-deflation algorithm** (content deflated by `BorderThickness + Padding`, matching WPF `MeasureOverride`/`ArrangeOverride`) are WPF-faithful and recorded HOLDS (pinned in S1130). 11bl owns ONLY what no other step owns:
> - **D1 (MATERIAL — the core defect) — `Background` is entirely absent as a Border DP AND as a render surface; WPF Border both ADDS the `Background` owned-DP and FILLS the interior.** WPF `Border.cs`: `BackgroundProperty = Panel.BackgroundProperty.AddOwner(typeof(Border), ...)` (the `AddOwner` chain — `(Background, Border)` is an OWNED DP whose owner-type is `Border`), and `Border.OnRender` fills the interior (`dc.DrawRectangle(background, null, new Rect(ptTL, ptBR))` simple path; the complex `DrawGeometry(borderBrush-background split)` at the `_useComplexRenderCodePath` fold). VAML's `register_border_properties()` registers only `BorderBrush`, `BorderThickness`, `CornerRadius`, `Padding` — NO `(Background, Border)` DP, NO `set_background()`/`background()` accessor, and the classifier emits a bare hollow `border_rect` (a ring) with NO interior fill. An authored `<Border Background="...">` neither resolves as a Border-owned DP nor renders a fill. **Is it covered elsewhere?** S643a/S643b parse `Border Background="#80RRGGBB"` and carry a Brush ON the authored `(Background, Border)` DP-name the reader resolves under composite identity (11k-8/11k-9 list `Background` as a Border own-DP in the target tables), but NO sprint registers or renders it. **Conversion blocker:** a faithful VAML cannot express WPF's signature filled `<Border Background="...">`, and the renderer has no interior-fill path for it.
> - **D2 (MATERIAL) — non-uniform `BorderThickness` is collapsed to a single "representative" edge; WPF strokes each edge with its own pen + a complex-geometry path.** WPF `Border.cs` strokes each edge independently with its own cached pen (`LeftPenCache`/`RightPenCache`/`TopPenCache`/`BottomPenCache`) and uses a **complex geometry path** for non-uniform thickness + rounded corners (`_useComplexRenderCodePath = (!border.IsUniform || (cornerRadius != null && !cornerRadius.IsUniform) || ...)`). VAML's classifier comment says "a 4-edge thickness uses the top as the representative stroke" and `border_rect`'s `thickness01` is a single SCALAR — the S205 shader is a single-band SDF that CANNOT express per-edge thickness. `BorderThickness="1,2,3,4"` cannot be rendered WPF-faithfully.
> - **D3 (VALUE-TYPE + RENDER) — `CornerRadius` is typed as WPF's dedicated `CornerRadius` STRUCT, not a generic `Thickness`; and non-uniform corners are not representable.** WPF `Border.cs:148` registers `CornerRadiusProperty` `typeof(CornerRadius)` — a struct with `TopLeft`/`TopRight`/`BottomLeft`/`BottomRight` + `IsUniform` + the `IsCornerRadiusValid` guard that REJECTS negative radii. VAML registers it `ValueType::Thickness` (no four-corner semantics, no negative-rejection) and the S205 shader supports only a UNIFORM `radius01` scalar — non-uniform corners are not representable, and a negative CornerRadius does NOT throw the WPF validation.
> - **D4 (RENDER) — null/zero-thickness Border draws NOTHING in WPF; VAML forcibly draws an opaque black ring + a phantom 1px band.** WPF `Border.cs`: the default `BorderBrush` metadata is `(Brush)null` and `OnRender` gates the band on `if (!border.IsZero && (borderBrush = BorderBrush) != null)` — when `BorderBrush` is null OR `BorderThickness` is zero, WPF draws NO border band. VAML's default `BorderBrush` is a shared OPAQUE BLACK brush (`default_black_brush()`), so a bare `<Border>` draws a black ring where WPF draws NONE; and the classifier FORCES `thickness01` to **at least 1.0 when `bt.top == 0`** (`(bt.top > 0 ? bt.top : 1.0f)`), so a zero-thickness Border renders an artificial 1px band WPF would never draw. Neither is scheduled.
> - **D5 (METADATA) — the WPF `Affects*`/`SubPropertiesDoNotAffectRender` framework flags on the Border DP set are not carried.** WPF registers `Padding`/`CornerRadius` with `AffectsMeasure | AffectsRender`, `BorderThickness` with `AffectsMeasure | AffectsRender`, `BorderBrush` with `AffectsRender | SubPropertiesDoNotAffectRender`, `Background` with `AffectsRender | SubPropertiesDoNotAffectRender`. VAML registers all four Border DPs with `PropertyFlags::None`. 11aa S818 delivered the `Affects*` invalidation ENGINE + the honoring `FrameworkElement.OnPropertyChanged` seam, but no sprint applied those flags to the S481 Border set — a Border-DP change does NOT carry WPF's declared measure/render invalidation.
> - **D6-PIN (what HOLDS — recorded NOT re-audited as drift, pinned in the gate):** the composite `(name, ownerType=Border)` DP identity (Rule 3), the `BorderBrush`/`BorderThickness`/`Padding`/`CornerRadius` owner-name registrations under owner `"Border"` matching WPF `typeof(Border)`, the **single-child content slot**, and the **measure/arrange combined-deflation algorithm** — all WPF-faithful and pinned, NOT re-litigated.

> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint — the contract forces full close, no scoped option):** (1) register `(Background, Border)` as an OWNED Brush DP via the `AddOwner` semantics of `Panel.BackgroundProperty` (the composite `(name="Background", owner="Border")` store key, per Rule 3 + 11s), with `set_background()`/`background()` accessors + `PropertyFlags::AffectsRender | SubPropertiesDoNotAffectRender` (11aa S818), and make the classifier emit the INTERIOR FILL (a `SolidRect` under the `BorderRect`, or extend `border_rect` with an interior fill at the WPF `new Rect(ptTL, ptBR)` deflated-by-border area); (2) non-uniform `BorderThickness` renders per-edge (the `border_rect`/`border_style` gained per-edge thickness + the complex-geometry path when `!IsUniform` OR non-uniform corners, mirroring `_useComplexRenderCodePath`); (3) `CornerRadius` is re-typed to a dedicated `CornerRadius` struct type (four corners + `IsUniform` + the `IsCornerRadiusValid` negative-rejection throwing per the 11t `S810_1` disposition) and non-uniform corners render via the complex-geometry path; (4) the null/zero-thickness render contract is honored — default `BorderBrush = nullptr` (WPF `(Brush)null`), the border band draws ONLY when `!IsZero && BorderBrush != null` (WPF `OnRender` gate), and the artificial `bt.top<1 -> 1px` fallback is REMOVED; (5) the Border DP set carries the WPF `Affects*`/`SubPropertiesDoNotAffectRender` framework flags consumed by the 11aa S818 invalidation seam. Each closes the exact drift; no invented surface is added; the WPF source (`Border.cs`) is the authority (Rule 1/Rule 2 held; Rule 3 held — all DPs key `(name, ownerType=Border)` per the 11s composite store).

## Sprint 11h --- 3rd-party IMPORT / INJECT seam  (goal: hard goal 3 — import and inject a 3rd-party control, proven in the viewer)  [token S520+]

> HARD GOAL 3 (sealed): to close out the lib we implement a means of importing 3rd-party libs and/or DLLs.
> Likely ONE sprint. We pick something we can put in a lib and INJECT, and the last step vaml_viewer shows the
> 3rd-party works.
>
> **FOREIGN-TYPE ACCESS MODEL (RECORDED DECISION — the "translation, not conversion" contract, resolved against
> the WPF source at plan review).** This is NOT a new sprint and NOT app-side conversion — VAML is a *reader*:
> it consumes the exact `clr-namespace:...;assembly=...` markup every in-box WPF app references, unchanged. The
> user's `.xaml` is NEVER edited to a "VAML format" — `clr-namespace` is already tokenized at S082 into
> `ClrNamespaceReference{clrNamespace, assembly}`; only the *resolution* of that reference is at issue, and it
> splits on whether the foreign type is platform-fixed or user-chosen:
> - **TIER 3a — IN-THE-BOX FRAMEWORK foreign types (LABEL-EQUIVALENT, in the LIB):** in-box reference-type
>   surface — `PresentationFramework.Aero2/AeroLite` (`SystemDropShadowChrome`), `System.Runtime`/`mscorlib`
>   primitives (`system:String.Empty`, `<system:Double>`, `<sys:Boolean>`), the `Microsoft.Windows.Themes`
>   types — is **platform-frozen, present in every WPF app, and NOT a NuGet choice**. It is the *same class as
>   `Label`*, which the lib already hardcodes as first-class. Therefore tier 3a lives in **vaml-core's S087
>   built-in registration table**, resolved **AUTOMATICALLY** — the same code path as `Label`, zero app action,
>   zero registration, zero install. This is the "access for free" path.
> - **TIER 2 — the RESOLVER SEAM (S520/11h), and TIER 3b — THIRD-PARTY toolkits (a plugin, NOT the lib):**
>   NuGet-package types (`DotNetProjects.Input.Toolkit` AutoCompleteBox, `MaterialDesignThemes.Wpf`) are
>   **unbounded + drifting + consumer-chosen** — the lib must NOT hardcode them (Label is platform-frozen; a
>   NuGet package is not). They resolve through the S520 `vaml::inject` seam: the app's `.xaml` STILL never

## Sprint 11z — Injected-dispatcher interop + injected-dispatch wrap  (goal: the library runs inside a host message pump / dispatcher; the 3rd-party test + injected test dispatch CLOSE OUT the lib roadmap)  [token S540+]
> VIEWER GROWTH: this sprint's NEW renderable/interop proof = S545 (an injected test dispatch, triggered via the
> 3rd-party test hook, updates UI content LIVE in the viewer) — the anti-grave-whistle wrap that closes out the lib.
>
> DESIGN FRAME (consistent with the "we do NOT impose a dispatcher/async runtime" decision, ADR-006
> app-owned composition): **this library does
> NOT require a dispatcher nor use one.** It must function inside an ecosystem that DOES own one. The library
> therefore exposes a REPLACEABLE executor seam — `IUiExecutor` — that a HOST chooses to inject to claim
> ownership of the real UI thread's message pump. The question **"who owns the UI thread?"** is answered by
> the host: the default is library-driven (the framework drains its own queue via `IdleForOneTask`), but an
> app that already runs Win32/X11 pumps may inject `IUiExecutor` to drive our deferred work themselves. The
> executor is OWNED by the thread that owns the pump, exactly as the S037/S041/S143 thread-affinity model
> requires.
- S540 dep:S532  `IUiExecutor` (vaml/core, cross-platform) — the injectable UI-thread executor seam, the
      REPLACEABLE interop surface (a host injects it; the library never imposes a dispatcher). `NativeMessage`
      is an opaque cross-platform message carrier: Win32 = `MSG` (windows.h), Linux = `XEvent`-compatible
      backend struct `{ type, window, x, y, code, modifiers, timestamp }` (enum Type { other, mouse_move,
      mouse_button, key }); `#error Unsupported platform` for anything else. Interface: `UnhandledMsg(NativeMessage&)`
      (a native message the library did not handle, forwarded to the app to handle/forward), `IdleForOneTask()`
      (run AT MOST one ready task on the UI thread; return true iff one was consumed, false if none ready),
      `Awaken() noexcept` (THREAD-SAFE: wake the pump, including when it is waiting). REAL permanent public
      surface (NOT a STUB / NOT MINIMAL REAL), kept + extended by S541/S542. Absence of an executor = the
      library's own default pump behavior.
- S541 dep:S540  Windows pump adapter — `RunMessagePump(IUiExecutor*)`: the cooperatively-driven Win32
      message pump. Per turn: `PeekMessageW` (at most one) → `WM_QUIT` returns quit code → `WM_APP_WAKE_PUMP`
      (`WM_APP + 0x3A1`, posted by `Awaken()`) consumed as a wake (the work itself drains via
      `IdleForOneTask`) → `HandleLibraryMessage(msg)` if consumed else `executor->UnhandledMsg(msg)` (or
      `TranslateMessage`/`DispatchMessage` when no executor) → then `executor->IdleForOneTask()`. If nothing
      was ready, `GetMessageW` sleeps until a native message or `WM_QUIT` arrives — the cross-thread wakeup.
      The pure dispatch decision seams (the `processMessage` body) are headless-ctestable; the live pump is
      [both apps, not CI]. Completes the "an app that owns a Win32 pump can drive us" contract.
- S542 dep:S541  X11 pump adapter — `RunX11MessagePump(Display*, IUiExecutor*, X11Wakeup&)`: the
      cooperatively-driven Xlib/poll(2) pump. `X11Wakeup` is a self-pipe (pipe() in ctor, read-fd read side,
      `Signal()` noexcept write-one-byte from ANY thread — EAGAIN = a wake already pending, `Drain()` reads
      the pipe on the pump thread after readable; non-copyable). Per turn: `XPending`/`XNextEvent` (at most one)
      → `HandleLibraryEvent(event)` else `executor->UnhandledMsg(event)` (or `HandleDefaultXEvent` when no
      executor — Xlib has no generic Translate/Dispatch; routing unhandled events is app-specific) →
      `executor->IdleForOneTask()`. If nothing was ready, `poll(2)` on { xConnection, wakeup.ReadFd() } blocks
      until either an X event or a wake; poll error/hup → -1. The pure decision seams are headless-ctestable;
      the live pump is [both apps, not CI].
- S543 dep:S542  App-side executor consumable — the injected-executor consumer shape documented + proven:
      an `AppUiExecutor : IUiExecutor` (the X11 app side shown) holds an `X11Wakeup&`, `Awaken() noexcept`
      → `wakeup_.Signal()`, and supplies the app's `UnhandledMsg`/`IdleForOneTask`. Records the "who owns the
      UI thread?" contract: **an app that injects an executor OWNS the pump**; the library only drains via
      `IdleForOneTask()` and is woken via `Awaken()`. ADR-018: ZERO new locks — the wakeup is a lock-free
      signal (pipe write / posted thread message), the executor is single-thread-owned by the pump thread
      (the S037/S041/S143 affinity model). [ADR-006: the seam is app-owned + replaceable; the library does
      NOT ship an executor of its own.]
- S543_1 dep:S543  APP-OWNED-PUMP INBOUND SEAM — promote `HandleLibraryMessage(NativeMessage&)` (Win32) /
      `HandleLibraryEvent(...)` (X11) from internal pump helpers into PUBLIC library surface: the documented,
      headless-ctestable inbound entry an APP-owned main loop calls ONCE per native message/event, forwarding
      to the S540 `IUiExecutor` + draining via `IdleForOneTask()`/`Awaken()`. S541/S542 carry a one-line
      forward note (their internal call IS the body promoted public at S543_1 — supersede in place, no
      duplicate implementation). Records the pump-ownership contract with BOTH hosting modes: (1) VAML runs
      the pump (S541/S542) + calls the app's injected async (S540 `IUiExecutor`); (2) the APP runs the pump
      + calls the S543_1 inbound seam each message. ADR-018: ZERO new locks — single pump-thread owner, the
      S037/S041/S143 affinity model. NO-GAP: mode 2 becomes a named, resolvable contract, not an undocumented
      backdoor.
- S544 dep:S543  REFACTOR GATE(S11z): the injected-executor surface interops with the existing S323 input /
      S211 marshalling / S11z pump seams (a host may now drive our deferred work from its OWN
      pump, or keep our default); build + warning-clean + ctest GREEN both CI lanes (windows-msvc +
      ubuntu-clang); grep-audit: the `IUiExecutor`/`NativeMessage`/`X11Wakeup` seams are all REAL + consumed
      (no stub / no MINIMAL REAL / nothing orphaned). ADR-018: zero new locks sprints-wide.
- S545 dep:S544  INJECTED-DISPATCH WRAP (the hard-goal-4 close-out — the "calling the interface works" proof): the
      S521 in-repo test 3rd-party lib triggers a dispatched UI-content change — the test control's dispatch signal
      POSTS through the S540 `IUiExecutor::IdleForOneTask()` into the UI thread → a VM property updates → the S252
      `{Binding}` repaints the LIVE viewer content (the injected-dispatcher UI update, WPF's
      `Dispatcher.Invoke`-analogue). This PROVES a 3rd-party/async origin can drive UI content through the injected
